Adv. Marc. 3.19: lignum, crux, sepultura, resurrectio.
latin: Age nunc, si legisti penes Dauid: dominus regnauit a ligno, expecto quid intellegas. nisi forte lignarium aliquem regem significari (putes) Iudaeorum, et non Christum, qui exinde a passione ligni superata morte regnauit. etenim si mors ab Adam regnauit usque ad Christum, cur Christus non regnasse dicatur a ligno, ex quo crucis ligno mortuus regnum mortis exclusit? proinde et Esaias: quoniam, inquit, puer natus est nobis, — quid noui, si non de filio dei dicit? — et datus est nobis cuius imperium factum est super humerum ipsius. quis omnino regum insigne potestatis suae humero praefert et non aut capite diadema aut manu sceptrum aut aliquam propriae uestis notam? sed solus nouus rei nouorum aeuorum Christus Iesus nouae gloriae et potestatem et sublimitatem suam humero extulit, crucem scilicet, ut secundum superiorem prophetiam exinde dominus regnaret a ligno.

hoc lignum et Hieremias tibi insinuat, (de) dicturis praedicans Iudaeis: uenite, coiciamus lignum in panem eius, utique in corpus. sic enim dominus in euangelio quoque uestro reuelauit, panem corpus suum appellans, ut et hinc iam eum intellegas corporis sui figuram pani dedisse, cuius retro corpus in panem prophetes figurauit, ipso domino hoc sacramentum postea interpretaturo. si adhuc quaeris dominicae crucis praedicationem, satis iam tibi potest facere uicesimus primus psalmus, totam Christi continens passionem, canentis iam tunc gloriam suam: foderunt, inquit, manus meas et pedes. quae propria atrocia sunt crucis. et rursus, cum auxilium patris implorat: saluum, inquit, fac me ex ore leonis, utique mortis. et de cornibus unicornis humilitateru(meam.) de apicibus scilicet crucis, ut supra ostendimus. quam crucem nec ipse Dauid passus est nec ullus rex Iudaeorum, ne putes alterius alicuius (prophetari passionem quam eius,) qui solus a populo tam insigniter crucifixus est.

nunc et si omnes istas interpretationes respuerit et inriserit haeretica duritia, concedam illi nullam Christi crucem significari [me] a creatore, quia nec ex hoc probabit alium esse qui crucifixus est. nisi forte ostenderit hunc exitum eius a suo deo praedicatum, ut diuersitas passionum, ac per hoc etiam personarum, ex diuersitate praedicationum uindicetur. ceterum nec ipso Christo eius praedicato, nedum cruce ipsius, sufficit in meum Christum solius mortis prophetia. ex hoc enim, quod non est edita qualitas mortis, potuit et per crucem euenisse, tunc alii deputanda, si in . alium fuisset praedicatum. nisi si nec mortem uolet Christi mei prophetatam, quo magis erubescat, si suum quidem Christum mortuum adnuntiat, quem negat natum, meum uero mortalem negat, quem nascibilem confitetur. et mortem autem et sepulturam et resun-ectionem Christi mei una uoce Esaiae uolo ostendere dicentis: sepultura eius sublata de medio est. nec sepultus enim esset nisi mortuus, nec sepultura eius sublata de medio nisi per resurrectionem. denique subiecit: propterea multos ipse hereditati habebit et multorum diuidet spolia pro eo, quod tradita est anima eius in mortem. ostensa enim causa gratiae huius, pro iniuria scilicet mortis sandae. pariter ostensum est haec illum [propter mortem consecuturum] post mortem, utique per resurrectionem, consecuturum.

author: Tertullian
english: Let the heretic learn — and the Jew too, with whom he may abound — the reason also of that one’s errors, from whom he borrowed lead in this argument, blind from blind, and fell into the same pit. We say two habits of Christ shown by the prophets marked as many advents of his: one in humility, of course the first, when he had to be led like a sheep to the victim and like a lamb before the shearer without voice, so not opening the mouth — not even honest in look. For we announced, he says, about him: like a little child, like a root in thirsty ground. And there is no appearance of him nor glory, and we saw him. And he had no appearance nor beauty, but his appearance was dishonored, failing short of the sons of men — a man in blow and knowing how to bear weakness — set by the Father as a stone of offense and rock of scandal, lessened by him a little under the angels, pronouncing himself a worm and not a man, mankind’s shame and the people’s nullifying.

These proofs of lowliness fit the first advent as those of height fit the second, when he will already be not a stone of offense nor rock of scandal, but the chief corner stone taken up after rejection and raised to the temple’s completion — the church, of course — and that rock in Daniel cut from the mountain, which will smash and crush the image of the world’s kingdoms. Of which advent the same prophet: And behold, coming with the clouds of heaven like a son of man he came to the ancient of days. He was present in his sight, and those standing by brought him. And royal power was given him and all nations of the earth by kinds and all glory in service. And his power forever which will not be taken away, and his kingdom which will not be spoiled.

Then of course he will have an honorable appearance and beauty that does not fail above the sons of men — for timely, he says, in beauty beyond the sons of men, grace is poured on your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever. Gird the sword on your thigh, powerful in your timing and beauty — when the Father also, after he lessened him a little under the angels, will crown him with glory and honor and put all under his feet. Then also those who pierced him will recognize him and beat their breasts tribe by tribe — of course because earlier they did not recognize him in the humility of the human condition: And he is a man, says Jeremiah, and who will know him? Because also: His nativity, Isaiah, who, he says, will tell? So also in Zechariah in Jesus’ person — indeed in the sacrament of the name itself — the Father’s true high priest, Christ Jesus, is outlined in a double habit into two advents: first clothed in filth, that is the unworthiness of passible and mortal flesh, when the devil also opposed him — author of course of Judas the traitor, not to say also tempter after baptism — then stripped of former filths and adorned with robe and mitre and clean turban, that is the glory and honor of the second advent. For if I also interpret the two goats offered on the fast, do not they too figure either order of Christ? Alike and similar for the same look of the Lord, because he will not come in another form, so that he may be recognized by those who hurt him. But one of them, wrapped in scarlet, cursed and spat on and torn and pierced, was cast by the people outside the city into ruin, marked with clear badges of the Lord’s passion; the other, offered for sins and given as food to the temple priests, signed the proofs of the second showing, by which, all sins expiated, the priests of the spiritual temple — that is the church — would enjoy the Lord’s grace as by a kind of feast, while the rest fast from salvation. Therefore since the first advent was sung both much veiled by figures and laid low by every dishonor, but the second both clear and worthy of God, they were not wrongly deceived who, looking only at the one easy to understand and believe — that is the second — missed the more obscure, certainly more unworthy — that is the first. And so to this day they deny their Christ has come, because he did not come in height, while they do not know he was also going to come in humility.
translator_notes: Source-locked to OGL/CSEL Adversus Marcionem opp-lat2.
latin: Discat nunc haereticus ei abundanti cum ipso licebit Iudaeo rationem quoque errorum eius, a quo ducatum mutuatus in hac argumentatione, caecus a caeco, in eandem decidit foueam. duos dicimus Christi habitus a prophetis demonstratos totidem aduentus eius praenotasse: unum in humilitate, utique primum, cum tamquam ouis ad uictimam deduci habebat et tamquam agnus ante tondentem sine uoce, ita non aperiens os. ne aspectu quidem honestus. adnuntiauimus enim, inquit. de illo: sicut puerulus, sicut radix in terra sitienti. et non est species eius neque gloria, et uidimus eum. et non habebat speciem neque decorem, sed species eius inhonorata, deficiens citra filios hominum, homo in plaga et sciens ferre infirmitatem, ut positus a patre in lapidem offensionis et petram scandali, minoratus ab eo modicum citra angelos, uermem se pronuntians et non hominem, ignominiam hominis et nullificamen populi.

quae ignobilitatis argumenta primo aduentui competunt sicut sublimitatis secundo, cum fiet iam non lapis offensionis nec petra scandali, sed lapis summus angularis post reprobationem adsumptus et sublimatus in consummationem templi, ecclesiae scilicet, et petra sane illa apud Danihelem de monte praecisa, quae imaginem saecularium regnorum comminuet et conteret. de quo aduentu idem prophetes: et ecce cum nubibus caeli tamquam filius hominis ueniens uenit usque ad ueterem dierum. aderat in conspectu eius, et qui adsistebant adduxerunt illum. et data est ei potestas regia et omnes nationes terrae secundum genera et omnis gloria famulabunda. et potestas eius usque in aeuum quae non auferetur, et regnum eius quod non uitiabitur.

tunc scilicet habiturus est speciem honorabilem et decorem indeficientem super filios hominum, - tempestiuus enim, inquit, decore citra filios hominum, effusa est gratia in labiis tuis; propterea benedixit te deus in aeuum. accingere ensem super femur tuum, potens tempestiuitate tua et pulchritudine tua — cum et pater, posteaquam diminuit eum modicum quid citra angelos, gloria et honore coronabit illum et subiciet omnia pedibus eius. tunc et cognoscent eum qui compugerunt et caedent pectora sua tribus ad tribum, utique quod retro non agnouerunt eum in humilitate condicionis humanae: et homo est, inquit Hieremias, et quis cognoscet illum? quia et: natiuitatem eius, Esaias, quis, inquit, enarrabit? sic et apud Zachariam in persona Iesu, immo et in ipso nominis sacramento, uerus summus sacerdos patris, Christus Iesus, duplici habitu in duos aduentus deliniatur, primo sordidis indutus, id est carnis passibilis et mortalis indignitate, cum et diabolus aduersabatur ei. auctor scilicet Iudae traditoris, ne dicam etiam post baptisma temptator, dehinc despoliatus pristinas sordes et exornatus podere et mitra et cidari munda, id est secundi aduentus gloria et honore. si enim et duorum hircorum, qui ieiunio offerebantur, faciam interpretationem, nonne et illi utrumque ordinem Christi figurant? pares quidem atque consimiles propter eundem domini conspectum, quia non in alia uenturus est forma, ut qui agnosci habeat a quibus laesus est. alter autem eorum circumdatus coccino, maledictus et consputatus et conuulsus et compunctus, a populo extra ciuitatem abiciebatur in perditionem, manifestis notatus insignibus dominicae passionis, alter uero pro delictis oblatus et sacerdotibus templi in pabulum datus secundae repraesentationis argumenta signabat, qua delictis omnibus expiatis sacerdotes templi spiritalis, id est ecclesiae, dominicae gratiae quasi uisceratione quadam frueren tur, ieiunantibus ceteris a salute. igitur quoniam primus aduentus et plurimum figuris obscuratus et omni inhonestate prostratus canebatur, secundus uero et manifestus et deo condignus. idcirco, quem facile et intellegere et credere potuerunt, eum solum intuentes, id est secundum, non inmerito decepti sunt: circa obscuriorem, certe indigniorem, id est primum. atque ita in hodiernum negant uenisse Christum suum, quia non in sublimitate uenerit, dum ignorant etiam in humilitate fuisse uenturum.

author: Tertullian
english: We also confess the letter that teaches the Galatians as the chief letter against Judaism. For we embrace that whole removal of the old law, as itself coming from the Creator’s arrangement — as we have often already treated in this order about the renewal preached by our God’s prophets. But if the Creator promised the old things would yield, with new of course about to rise, and Christ marked the time of that departure — the law and the prophets until John — setting the boundary in John between either order of old things ending from then and new beginning, necessarily the apostle also, in Christ revealed after John, weakens the old and confirms the new, and so cares for the faith of no other god than the Creator’s, with whom also the old things were preached as about to depart.

Therefore both the law’s destruction and the gospel’s building work for me in this letter too, bearing on that presumption of the Galatians by which they presumed Christ, as if the Creator’s, had to be believed with the Creator’s law kept — because it still seemed incredible that the law be laid down by its own author. Further, if they had heard from the apostle an altogether other god, they would of course have known of themselves that they must withdraw from that god’s law whom they had left by following another. For who would wait longer to learn that he ought to follow a new discipline who had received a new god? No: because the same divinity was preached in the gospel that had always been known in the law, but not the same discipline, this was the whole state of the question: whether the Creator’s law ought to be shut out from the gospel in the Creator’s Christ.

Take away this state, and the question is empty. And with the question empty — everyone of themselves recognizing they must leave the Creator’s order by faith in another god — no material would have suited the apostle for teaching so tightly what faith itself would have dictated of its own. Therefore this letter’s whole intent teaches nothing other than the law’s departure coming from the Creator’s arrangement, as we will still suggest. If likewise it puts out mention of no new god — which it would nowhere have done more than in this matter, so as to propose the reason for sending the law away by this sole and most sufficient definition of a new divinity — it appears how he writes: I marvel that you are so quickly transferred from him who called you into grace to another gospel — another from way of life, not from religion; from discipline, not from divinity — since indeed Christ’s gospel ought to call from the law to grace, not from the Creator to another god.
translator_notes: Source-locked to OGL/CSEL Adversus Marcionem opp-lat2.
latin: Principalem aduersus Iudaismum epistolam nos quoque confitemur quae Galatas docet. amplectimur etenim omnem illam legis ueteris amolitionem, ut et ipsam de creatoris uenientem dispositione, sicut saepe iam in isto ordine tractauimus de praedicata nouatione a prophetis dei nostri. quodsi creator quidem uetera cessura promisit, nouis scilicet orituris, Christus uero tempus distinx(it decess)ionis istius, — lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem — terminum in Iohanne statuens inter utrumque ordinem desinentium exinde ueterum et incipientium nouorum, necessarie et apostolus in Christo post Iohannem reuelato uetera infirmat, noua uero confirmat, atque ita non alterius dei fidem curat quam creatoris, apud quem et uetera decessura praedicabantur.

igitur et legis destructio et euangelii aedificatio pro me faciunt in ista quoque epistola ad eam Galatarum praesumptionem pertinentes, qua praesumebant Christum, ut puta creatoris, salua creatoris lege credendum, quod adhuc incredibile uideretur legem a suo auctore deponi. porro, si omnino alium deum ab apostolo audissent, ultro utique scissent abscedendum sibi esse a lege eius dei, quem reliquissent alium secuti. quis enim expectaret diutius discere, quod nonam deberet sectari disciplinam qui nouum deum recepisset? immo quia eadem quidem diuinitas praedicabatur in euangelio, quae semper nota fuerat in lege, disciplina uero non eadem, hic erat totus quaestionis status, an lex creatoris ab euangelio deberet excludi in Christo creatoris.

denique aufer hunc statum, et uacat quaestio. uacante autem quaestione, ultro omnibus agnoscentibus discedendum sibi esse ab ordine creatoris per fidem dei alterius, nulla apostolo materia competisset id tam presse doctadi, quod ultro fides ipsa dictasset. igitur tota intentio epistolae istius nihil aliud docet quam legis decessionem uenientem de creatoris dispositione, ut adhuc suggeremus. si item nullius noui dei exerit mentionem, quod nusquam magis fecisset quam in ista materia, ut rationem scilicet ablegandae legis unica hac et sufficientissima definitione proponeret nouae diuinitatis, apparet quomodo scribat: miror uos tam cito transferri ab eo, qui uos uocauit in gratiam, ad aliud euangelium, ex conuersatione aliud, non ex religione, ex disciplina, non ex diuinitate, quoniam quidem euangelium Christi a lege euocare deberet ad gratiam, non a creatore ad alium deum.

author: Tertullian
english: The Lord’s burier also ought to have been prophesied and already then worthily blessed, if prophecy does not pass by those women’s office who before light gathered at the tomb with a preparation of spices. For of this through Hosea: And they will seek, he says, my face; before light they will watch for me saying: Let us go and turn to the Lord, because he himself has seized and will heal us, he struck and will pity us, he will heal us after two days, on the third day we will rise.

For who would not believe these things rolled in those women’s thought between the pain of present forsaking, by which they seemed to themselves struck by the Lord, and the hope of his resurrection, by which they thought they would be restored? And with the body not found, his burial had been taken up from the midst according to Isaiah. But also two angels appeared there — about as many side-helpers as God’s word was used to stand on in two witnesses. Isaiah also foresaw the women returning from the tomb and from that angels’ vision: Women, he says, coming from the vision, come — to announce of course the Lord’s resurrection. And it is well that the disciples’ unbelief persisted, so that to the end our defense would stand: that Christ had shown himself to the disciples as no other than the prophets’. For when two of them were on the way and the Lord had joined them, not appearing as himself, even hiding knowledge of what was done: But we thought, they say, he was Israel’s redeemer — of course their Christ, that is the Creator’s. So he had not shown himself as another to them. Otherwise they would not have thought him the Creator’s; and when he was thought the Creator’s, he would not have borne this thought about himself if he were not the one thought. Else he himself will be author of error and traitor of truth against the best God’s title. But not even after the resurrection did he show himself to them as other than whom they had said they thought. Clearly he attacked them: O senseless and slow of heart in not believing all that he spoke to you. What things spoken? That he was of another god? Prove it, and I yield. Or the same things the angels also to the women: Remember what he spoke to you in Galilee, saying that the Son of man must be handed over and crucified and rise on the third day? And why must it, unless because so it was written by God the Creator? Therefore he rebuked them as scandalized only at the passion and as doubtful of the faith of the resurrection announced to them by the women — by which they had not believed he was the very one they had thought. So what they had thought, that he wanted believed: he confirmed himself as the one they had thought — of course the Creator’s Christ, Israel’s redeemer.

But what can be clearer about the truth of the body? When they hesitated lest he be a phantasm — indeed believing a phantasm: Why are you troubled? he says, and why do thoughts enter your hearts? See my hands and my feet, because I myself am, since a spirit does not have bones as you see me having. And Marcion, I believe by industry, was unwilling to erase from his gospel certain things contrary to himself, so that from those he could erase and did not erase, those he did erase may either be denied erased or said rightly erased; nor does he spare except those he overturns no less by interpreting otherwise than by deleting. So he wants it said thus: A spirit does not have bones as you see me having — as if as you see me having were referred to the spirit, that is not having bones, as the spirit also. And what reason for this twist, when he could have pronounced simply: because a spirit does not have bones as you see me not having? But why does he offer their inspection his hands and feet, which members consist of bones, if he had no bones? Why add: And know that I am — whom of course they had known before as bodily? Or if he was a phantasm through and through, why rebuke them for believing a phantasm? Yet while they still did not believe he desired food for this reason: to show he even had teeth. We have fulfilled, I think, the pledge. We have exhibited the law’s Christ by the prophets’ teachings, sentences, affections, senses, powers, passions, even resurrection as no other than the Creator’s — since also sending apostles to preach to all nations he commanded, fulfilling the psalm, that their sound go out into all the earth and their voices to the ends of the earth. I pity you, Marcion; you have labored in vain. For Christ Jesus in your gospel is mine.
translator_notes: Source-locked to OGL/CSEL Adversus Marcionem opp-lat2.
Adv. Marc. 4.43: sepulcrum, resurrectio, phantasma, creator.
latin: Oportuerat etiam sepultorem domini prophetari ac iam tunc merito benedici, si nec mulierum illarum officium praeterit prophetia, quae ante lucem conuenerunt ad sepulcrum cum odorum paratura. de hoc enim per Osee: et quaerent, inquit, faciem meam; ante lucem uigilabunt ad me dicentes: eamus et conuertamur ad dominum, quia ipse eripuit [dixit] et curabit nos, percussit et miserebitur nostri, sanabit nos post biduum, in die tertia resurgemus.

quis enim haec non credat in recogitatu mulierum illarum uolutata inter dolorem praesentis destitutionis, qua percussae sibi uidebantur a domino, et spem resurrectionis ipsius, qua restitutuiri se arbitrabantur? corpore autem non inuento sublata erat sepultura eius de medio secundum Esaiam. sed et duo ibidem angeli apparuerunt. tot fere laterensibus uti solebat in duobus testibus consistens dei sermo. reuertentes quoque a sepulcro mulieres et ab illa angelorum uisione prospiciebatEsaias: mulieres, inquit, [uenite] uenientes a uisione, uenite, ad renuntiandam scilicet domini resurrectionem. Bene autem,I quod incredulitas discipulorum perseuerabat, ut in finem usque defensio nostra consisteret Christum legum non alium se discipulis edidisse quam prophetarum. nam cum duo ex illis iter agerent et dominus eis adhaesisset, non comparens quod ipse esset, etiam dissimulans de conscientia rei gestae: nos autem putabamus, inquiunt, ipsum esse redemptorem Israhelis, utique suum Christum, id est creatoris. adeo nec alium se ediderat illis. ceterum non existimarent eum creatoris,I et cum creatoris existimaretur, non sustinuisset hanc de se existimationem, si non is esset, qui existimabatur. aut ipse! erit auctor erroris et praeuaricator ueritatis aduersus dei optimi titulum. sed nec post resurrectionem alium se eis ostendit quam quem existimatum sibi dixerant. plane inuectus est in illos: o insensati et tardi corde in non credendo omnibus, quae locutus est ad uos. quaenam locutus? alterius se dei esse? proba, et manus dedo. an eadem et angeli ad mulieres: rememoramini, quae locutus sit uobis in Galilaea dicens, quod oportet tradi filium hominis et crucifigi et tertia die resurgere? et quare oportebat, nisi quia ita a deo creatore scriptum? igitur increpuit illos ut de sola passione scandalizatos et ut dubios de fide resurrectionis adnuntiatae sibi a feminis, per quae non crediderant ipsum fuisse, quem existimauerant. itaque quod existimauerant, id uolens credi se eum se confirmabat, quem existimauerant, creatoris scilicet Christum, redemptorem Israhelis.

De corporis autem ueritate quid potest clarius? cum haesitantibus eis, ne phantasma esset, immo phantasma credentibus: quid turbati estis? (in quit,) et quid cogitationes subeunt in corda uestra? uidete manus meas et pedes, quia ipse ego sum, quoniam spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me habentem uidetis. et Marcion quaedam contraria sibi illa, credo, industria eradere de euangelio suo noluit, ut ex his, quae eradere potuit nec erasit, illa, quae erasit, aut negetur erasisse aut merito erasisse dicatur; nec parcit nisi eis, quae non minus aliter interpretando quam delendo subuertit. uult itaque sic dictum: spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me uidetis habentem, quasi ad spiritum referatur sicut me uidetis habentem, id est non habentem ossa, sicut et spiritus. et quae ratio tortuositatis istius, cum simpliciter pronuntiare potuisset:. quia spiritus ossa non habet, sicut me uidetis non habentem? cur autem inspectui eorum manus et pedes suos offert, quae membra ex ossibus constant, si ossa non habebat? cur adicit: et scitote, quia ego sum, quem scilicet corporeum retro nouerant? aut si phantasma erat usquequaque, cur illos phantasma credentes increpabat? atquin adhuc eis non credentibus propterea cibum desiderauit, ut se ostenderet etiam dentes habere. Impleuimus, ut opinor, sponsionem. exhibuimus legum Christum prophetarum doctrinis sententiis adfectibus sensibus uirtutibus passionibus etiam resun-ectione non alium quam creatoris, siquidem et apostolos mittens ad praedicandum uniuersis nationibus in omnem terram exire sonum eorum et in terminos terrae uoces eorum psalmum adimplendo praecepit. misereor tui, Marcion; frustra laborasti. Christus enim Iesus in euangelio tuo meus est.

author: Tertullian
english: So when the goodness of God himself had looked ahead to man for knowing God, it also added this to its own proclamation: that it first designed for man a dwelling — some greatest mass, and afterward also a greater — so that in the great he might practice and grow as in a lesser and so be advanced from God’s good, that is the great, also to his best, that is the greater dwelling. For the good work it also employs the best servant, his Word: My heart, he says, has uttered a best word. Let Marcion recognize from here first the best fruit, of course of the best tree. A most ignorant rustic indeed has grafted a bad into a good. But the shoot of blasphemy will not hold; it will dry with its craftsman, and so the nature of the good tree will testify to itself.

Look to the sum: what sort of things the Word has fruited: And God said, Let it be, and it was, and God saw that it was good — not as if not knowing the good unless he saw, but because it was good, therefore seeing, honoring and sealing and checking off the goodness of the works by the dignity of his gaze. So also he was blessing what he was doing well, so that the whole God would be recommended to you, good both to speak and to do. The Word still did not know how to speak ill, because neither to do ill. We will see the causes that also required this from God. Meanwhile the world stood from all goods, showing enough how much good was being prepared for the one for whom this whole was prepared. Who finally is worthy to inhabit God’s works other than his own image and likeness?

That too goodness — and a more working goodness — worked: not by an imperial word but by a familiar hand, even with a coaxing word first: Let us make man toward our image and likeness. Goodness spoke; goodness shaped from mud into so great a substance of flesh, built from one matter into so many qualities; goodness breathed into a soul, not dead but living; goodness set him over all things to enjoy and rule, even to name; goodness further added delights for man so that, though possessing the whole world, he might stay in more pleasant places, transferred into paradise — already then from the world into the church —; the same goodness also looked ahead to a helper, lest anything not be good. For it is not, he says, good for the man to be alone. It knew the sex of Mary would profit him and afterward the church. But even the law you accuse, which you twist into controversies, goodness laid on, consulting for man so he would cling to God, lest he seem not so much free as cast off, to be equated with his servants, the other animals, loose from God and free from disdain — but so that man alone would glory that he alone had been worthy to take a law from God, and so that a rational animal, capable of understanding and knowledge, would also be held by rational freedom itself, subject to him who had subjected all things to him. The counsel of observing that law goodness likewise wrote on: But on the day you eat, you will die by death. Most kindly it showed the exit of transgression, lest ignorance of the danger aid neglect of obedience. Further, if the reason for imposing the law went first, there also followed that of observing it, so that a penalty would be written for transgression — which yet he who predicted it beforehand did not want to happen. Recognize therefore the goodness of our God at least this far from good works, from good blessings, from indulgences, from providences, from laws and good and kind forewarnings.

Adv. Marc. 2.4: bonitas, imago, lex, praemonitio.
latin: Igitur cum cognoscendo deo hominem prospexisset bonitas dei ipsius, etiam hoc praeconio suo addidit, quod prius domicilium homini commentata est aliquam [postmodum] molem maximam, postmodum et maiorem, ut in magna tamquam in minore proluderet atque proficeret et ita de bono dei, id est de magno, ad optimum quoque eius, id est ad maius habitaculum, promoueretur. adhibet operi bono optimum etiam ministrum, sermonem suum: eructauit, inquit, cor meum sermonem optimum. agnoscat hinc primum fructum optimum, utique optimae arboris, Marcion. imperitissimus rusticus quidem malam in bonam inseruit. sed non ualebit blasphemiae surculus; arescet cum suo artifice et ita se bonae arboris natura testabitur.

aspice ad summam, qualia sermo fructificauerit: et dixit deus: fiat, et factum est, et uidit deus quia bonum, non quasi nesciens bonum nisi uideret, sed quia bonum, ideo uidens, honorans et consignans et dispungens bonitatem operum dignatione conspectus. sic et benedicebat quae benefaciebat, ut tibi totus deus commendaretur, bonus et dicere et facere. male dicere adhuc sermo non norat, quia nec malefacere. uidebimus causas, quae hoc quoque a deo exegerunt. interim mundus ex bonis omnibus constitit, satis praemonstrans, quantum boni pararetur illi, cui praeparabatur hoc totum. quis denique dignus incolere dei opera quam ipsius imago et similitudo?

eam quoque bonitas et quidem operantior operata est, non imperiali uerbo, sed familiari manu, etiam uerbo blandiente praemisso: faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram. bonitas dixit; bonitas finxit de limo in tantam substantiam carnis, ex una materia tot qualitatibus exstructam; bonitas inflauit in animam, non mortuam, sed uiuam; bonitas praefecit uniuersis fruendis atque regnandis, etiam cognomiuandis; bonitas amplius delicias adiecit homini, ut, quamquam totius orbis . possidens, in amoenioribus moraretur, translatus in paradisum — iam tunc de mundo in ecclesiam —; eadem bonitas et adiutorium prospexit, ne quid non boni. non est enim, inquit, bonum solum esse hominem. sciebat illi sexum Mariae et deinceps ecclesiae profuturum. sed et quam arguis legem, quam in controuersias torques, bonitas irrogauit, consulens homini, quo deo adhaereret, ne non tam liber quam abiectus uideretur, aequandus famulis suis, ceteris animalibus, solutis a deo et ex fastidio liberis, sed ut solus homo gloriaretur, quod solus dignus fuisset, qui legem a deo sumeret, utque animal rationale, intellectus et scientiae capax, ipsa quoque libertate rationali contineretur, ei subiectus, qui subiecerat illi omnia. cuius legis obseruandae consilium bonitas pariter adscripsit: qua die autem ederitis, morte moriemini. benignissime enim demonstrauit exitum transgressionis, ne ignorantia periculi neglegentiam iuuaret obsequii. porro si legis imponendae ratio praecessit, sequebatur etiam obseruandae, ut poena transgressioni adscriberetur, quam tamen euenire noluit qui ante praedixit. agnosce igitur bonitatem dei nostri interim uel bucusque ex operibus bonis, ex benedictionibus bonis, ex indulgentiis, ex prouidentiis, ex legibus et praemonitionibus bonis et benignis.

author: Tertullian
english: It is enough to have run this far for now through Christ’s order, by which, proved such as he was announced, he ought to be held no other than the one who was announced such — so that already from this agreement of his deeds and the Creator’s scriptures faith also ought to be restored to those points by the prejudice of the greater part which, from a contrary opinion, are either drawn into doubt or denied. Further now we also build on equal things from the Creator’s scriptures that were sung ahead as about to be after Christ. For this arrangement too would not be found discharged if he had not come after whom it was to happen. Look at all the nations rising from then out of the gulf of human error toward God the Creator, toward God Christ. And if you dare, deny it was prophesied. But at once the Father’s promise in the psalms will meet you: You are my son; today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession. Nor can you claim David’s son more than Christ, or the ends of the earth promised rather to David — who reigned within the Jews’ single nation — than to Christ, who has already taken the whole world by the faith of his gospel.

So also through Isaiah: Behold, I have given you for an arrangement of the race, for a light of the nations, to open the eyes of the blind — of course of those erring — to loose the bound from chains, that is to free from sins, and those sitting in darkness from the prison-cell, that is of death, of ignorance of course. If these things happen through Christ, they will have been prophesied toward no other than him through whom they happen.

Likewise elsewhere: Behold, I have set him as a testimony to the nations, a prince and commander of nations; nations that do not know you will call on you, and peoples will flee to you. For you will not interpret these into David, because he first said: And I will arrange for you an eternal arrangement, the devout and faithful things of David. But from here rather you ought to understand Christ counted from David by fleshly line because of the virgin Mary’s census. For about this promise it is sworn in the psalm to David: From the fruit of your womb I will set on your throne. Whose womb is that? David’s own? Of course not — for David was not going to give birth. But not his wife’s either. For he would not have said “from the fruit of your womb,” but rather “from the fruit of your wife’s womb.” But by saying the womb itself, it remains that he pointed to someone of his line whose womb’s fruit would be Christ’s flesh, which flowered from Mary’s womb. And so he named only the fruit of the womb, as proper to the womb, as of the womb alone, not also of a man, and referred the womb itself back to David, to the head of the line and father of the family. For because he could not assign a virgin’s womb to a husband, he assigned it to the father. So what is found today as a new arrangement in Christ will be what the Creator then promised, calling Christ’s things the devout and faithful things of David, because Christ is from David. Indeed his flesh itself will be the devout and faithful things of David, so holy by religion and faithful from the resurrection. For Nathan the prophet too in the second of Kingdoms makes a profession to David of his seed: which will be, he says, from his own womb. If you simply expound this into Solomon, you will make me laugh. For David will seem to have given birth to Solomon. Or is Christ here too signified as David’s seed from that womb which would be from David — that is Mary’s? Because also Christ rather than Solomon was going to build God’s house — that is the holy man in whom as a better temple God’s Spirit would dwell — and Christ rather than Solomon, David’s son, would have to be God’s Son. Finally the throne forever and kingdom forever fit Christ more than Solomon, a temporal king of course. But from Christ God’s mercy did not withdraw; to Solomon even God’s anger came after luxury and idolatry. For he raised for him Satan an Idumaean enemy. Since therefore none of these fit Solomon but Christ, the reason of our interpretations will be sure, the very outcome of the things also proving them, which appear preached into Christ. And so in this will be the holy and faithful things of David; this one God set as a testimony to the nations, not David; a prince and commander of nations, not David, who ruled only Israel. Nations that did not know him call on Christ today, and peoples flee today to Christ whom they formerly ignored. What you see happening cannot be called future.

Adv. Marc. 3.20: gentes, Dauid, Maria, prophetiae.
latin: Sufficit hucusque de his interim ordinem Christi decucurrisse, quo talis probatus, qualiter adnuntiabatur, non alius haberi debeat quam qui talis adnuntiabatur, ut iam ex ista consonantia rerum eius et scripturarum creatoris illis etiam restituenda sit fides ei praeiudicio maioris partis, quae a diuersa sententia uel in dubium deducuntur uel negantur. amplius nunc superstruimus ea quoque paria ex scripturis creatoris, quae post Christum futura praecinebantur. nec (haec) enim dispositio expuncta inueniretur, si non ille uenisset, post quem habebat euenire. aspice uniuersas nationes de uoragine erroris humani exinde emergentes ad deum creatorem, ad deum Christum. et, si audes, nega prophetatum. sed statim tibi in psalmis promissio patris occurret: filius meus es tu, ego hodie generaui te. postula de me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam et possessionem tuam terminos terrae. nec poteris magis Dauid filium eius uindicare quam Christum, aut terminos terrae Dauid potius promissos. qui intra unicam Iudaeorum gentem regnauit, quam Christo. qui totum iam orbem euangelii sui fide cepit.

sic et per Esaiam: ecce dedi te in dispositionem generis, in lucem nationum, aperire oculos caecorum, utique errantium, exsoluere de uinculis uinctos, id est de delictis liberare, et de cella carceris, id est mortis, sedentes in tenebris, ignorantiae scilicet. quae si per Christum eueniunt, non in alium erunt prophetata quam per quem eueniunt.

item alibi: ecce testimonium eum nationibus posui, principem et imperantem nationibus; nationes, quae te non sciunt. inuocabunt te, et populi confugient ad te. nec enim haec in Dauid interpretaberis, quia praemisit: et disponam uobis dispositionem aeternam, religiosa et fidelia Dauid. atquin hinc magis Christum intellegere debebis ex Dauid deputatum carnali genere ob Mariae uirginis censum. de hoc enim promisso iuratur in psalmo ad Dauid: ex fructu uentris tui collocabo super thronum tuum. quis iste uenter est? ipsius Dauid? utique non. neque enim pariturus esset Dauid. sed nec uxoris eius. non enim dixisset: ex fructu uentris tui, sed potius: ex fructu uentris uxoris tuae. ipsius autem dicendo uentrem superest, ut aliquem de genere eius ostenderit, cuius uentris futurus esset fructus caro Christi, quae ex utero Mariae floruit. ideoque et fructum uentris tantum nominauit, ut proprie uentris, quasi solius uentris, non etiam uiri, et ipsum uentrem ad Dauid redegit, ad principem generis et familiae patrem. nam quia uiro deputare non poterat uirginis uentrem, patri eum deputauit. ita quae in Christo noua dispositio inuenitur hodie, haec erit, quam tunc creator pollicebatur, religiosa et fidelia Dauid appellans quae erant Christi, quia Christus ex Dauid. [immo ipsa erit caro eius religiosa et fidelia Dauid, tam sancta religione et fidelis ex resurrectione.] nam et Xathan propheta in secunda Basiliarum professionem ad Dauid facit semini eius: quod erit, inquit, ex uentre ipsius., hoc si in Salomonem simpliciter edisseres, risum mihi incuties. uidebitur enim Dauid peperisse Salomonem. an et hic Christus significatur ex eo uentre semen Dauid, qui esset ex Dauid. id est Mariae? quia et aedem dei magis Christus aedificaturus esset, hominem scilicet sanctum, in quo potiore templo inhabitaret dei spiritus, et in dei filium magis Christus haberet esse quam Salomon, filius Dauid. denique et thronus in aeuum et regnum in aeuum magis Christo competit quam Salomoni, temporali scilicet regi. sed (et) a Christo misericordia dei non abscessit, Salomoni uero etiam ira dei accessit post luxuriam et idolatriam. suscitauit enim illi Satan hostem Idumaeum. cum ergo nihil horum competat in Salomonem, sed in Christum, certa erit ratio interpretationum nostrarum, ipso etiam exitu rerum probante, quas in Christum apparet praedicatas. et ita in hoc erunt sancta et fidelia Dauid; hunc deus testimonium nationibus posuit, non Dauid, principem et imperantem nationibus, non Dauid, qui soli Israheli imperauit. Christum hodie inuocant nationes, quae eum non sciebant, et populi ad Christum hodie confugiunt, quem retro ignorabant. non pote::;t futurum dici quod uides fieri.

author: Tertullian
english: In this question, if you think the Creator’s angels should be set against us — as if they too acted with Abraham and Lot in a phantasm, of putative flesh of course, and yet truly met and ate and did what was commanded them — first you will not be admitted to examples of that God whom you destroy. For the better and more perfect a god you bring in, so much less do that one’s examples fit him, unless he will be different in the whole, altogether better and more perfect. Next know that this too is not granted you: that the flesh in the angels was putative, but of a true and solid human substance. For if it was not hard for him to show true senses and acts to putative flesh, he much more easily had it to give a true substance of flesh to true senses and acts — or as its own author and craftsman. For your god, because he produced no flesh at all, perhaps deservedly brought in its phantasm, whose truth he had not been able; but my God, who reformed that taken from mud into this quality — not yet from marital seed and yet flesh — could equally from any matter also have built flesh for angels, who even built the world from nothing into so many and such bodies, and by a word at that. And of course, if your god someday promises men the angels’ true substance — for they will be, he says, like angels — why should my God not also have fitted men’s true substance to angels, taken from wherever? Because you will not answer me either from where that angelic stuff with you is taken.

It is enough for me to define this, which fits God: namely the truth of that thing which he cast before three witnessing senses — sight, touch, hearing. It is harder for God to lie than to produce the truth of flesh from wherever, even if not born. But to other heretics too, defining that that flesh in the angels ought to have been born from flesh if it were truly human, we answer with a sure reason by which it both was truly human and unborn: truly human because of God’s truth, foreign to lying and deceit, and because they could not be treated in a human way by men except in a human substance; but unborn, because only Christ had to be born into flesh from flesh, so that by his nativity he would reform our nativity and so also by his death dissolve our death by rising in the flesh in which he was born, so that he could also die. And therefore he himself then with the angels appeared with Abraham in the truth of flesh indeed, but not yet born, because not yet about to die, but already learning to live among men.

So much the more angels, not arranged for dying for us, ought not to have taken a brief passage of flesh by being born, because they were not going to lay it down by dying. But from wherever taken and however altogether sent down, they still did not lie about it. If the Creator makes angels spirits and his attendants a burning fire — as truly spirits as also fire — the same one also truly made them flesh, so that we may now recall and announce to the heretics that the promise of someday reforming men into angels is his who once formed angels into men.

Adv. Marc. 3.9: phantasma, uera caro, natiuitas, resurrectio.
latin: In ista quaestione qui putaueris opponendos esse nobis angelos creatoris, quasi et illi in phantasmate, putatiuae utique carnis, egerint apud Abraham et Loth, et tamen uere sint et congressi et pasti et operati quod mandatum eis fuerat, primo non admitteris ad eius dei exempla, quem destruis. nam et quanto meliorem et perfectiorem deum inducis, tanto non competunt illi eius exempla, quo nisi diuersus in totum n<m erit omnino melior atque perfectior. dehinc scito nec illud concedi tibi, ut putatiua fuerit in angelis caro, sed uerae et solidae substantiae humanae. si enim difficile non fuit illi. putatiuae carni ueros et sensus et actus exhibere, multo facilius habuit, ueris et sensibus et actibus ueram dedisse substantiam carnis, uel qua proprius auctor et artifex eius. tuus enim deus eo, quod carnem nullam omnino produxerit, merito fortasse phantasma eius intulerit, cuius non ualuerat ueritatem, meus autem deus, qui illam de limo sumptam in hanc reformauit qualitatem, nondum ex semine coniugali et tamen carnem, aeque potuit ex quacumque materia angelis quoque adstruxisse carnem, qui etiam mundum ex nihilo in tot ac talia corpora, et quidem uerbo, aedificauit. et utique, si deus tuus ueram quandoque substantiam angelorum hominibus pollicetur, — erunt enim, inquit, sicut angeli — cur non et deus meus ueram substantiam hominum angelis accommodarit (unde)unde sumptam? quia nec tu mihi respondebis, unde illa apud te angelica sumatur.

sufficit mihi hoc definire, quod deo congruit, ueritatem scilicet eius rei, quam tribus testibus sensibus obiecit: uisui tactui auditui. difficilius deo mentiri quam carnis ueritatem (unde)unde producere, licet non natae. ceterum et aliis haereticis, definientibus carnem illam in angelis ex carne nasci debuisse, si uere fuisset humana, certa ratione respondemus, qua et humana uere fuerit et innata: humana uere propter dei ueritatem, a mendacio et fallacia extranei, et quia non possent humanitus tractari ab hominibus nisi in substantia humana; innata autem, quia solus Christus in carnem ex carne nasci habebat, ut natiuitatem nostram natiuitate sua reformaret atque ita etiam mortem nostram morte sua dissolueret resurgendo in carne, in qua natus est, ut et mori posset. ideoque et ipse cum angelis tunc apud Abraham in ueritate quidem carnis apparuit, sed nondum natae, quia nondum moriturae, sed ediscentis iam inter homines conuersari.

quo magis angeli, neque ad moriendum pro nobis dispositi, breuem carnis commeatum non debuerunt nascendo sumpsisse, quia nec moriendo deposituri eam fuerant. sed (unde)unde sumpta et quoquo modo omnino demissa, mentiti eam tamen non sunt. si creator facit angelos spiritus et apparitores suos ignem flagrantem, tam uere spiritus quam et ignem, idem illos uere fecit et carnem, ut nunc recordemur et haereticis renuntiemus eius esse promissum homines in angelos reformandi quandoque, qui angelos in homines formarit aliquando.

author: Tertullian
english: For these things, going back to console the fear of death and the sadness of dissolution itself, he is clear also through what follows, when he adds that we groan from this tent of an earthly body, longing to put on over it what is from heaven: since even stripped we will not be found naked — that is: we will receive what we were stripped of, that is the body — and again: for we who are in this tent of the body groan, being burdened, not willing to be stripped but to be clothed over. For here he expressed what he touched in the first letter: and the dead will rise incorrupt — who have already died — and we will be changed, who will have been caught in the flesh by God here. For those too will rise incorrupt, having received the body of course and indeed whole, so that from this they are incorrupt, and these, because of the last moment of time already and because of the deserts of antichrist’s harassings a shortcut of death, but changed, will follow, clothed over with what is from heaven rather than stripped of the body. So if these put that heavenly thing on over the body, of course the dead too will receive the body, over which they also put on incorruption from heaven, because he also says of them: This corruptible must put on incorruption and this mortal immortality. Those put on when they have received the body; these put on over, because they have not lost the body, and therefore he did not say rashly: not willing to be stripped of the body but clothed over — that is, not willing to experience death but to be anticipated by life, so that this mortal may be swallowed by life while it is snatched from death by the over-clothing of change. Therefore, because he showed this is better, lest we be saddened by death’s possible anticipation, he also says we have the Spirit’s earnest from God, as if pledged into the same hope of over-clothing, and are away from the Lord as long as we are in the flesh, and for that reason ought to count it good rather to be away from the body and be with the Lord, so that we may also receive death gladly. And so he says all of us must be shown before Christ’s tribunal, so that each may receive what he did through the body, whether good or evil. For if then is the repayment of deserts, how can some already be counted with the Lord? And by naming a tribunal and a sorting of good and evil work he showed a judge of either sentence and confirmed a bodily presentation of all. For what was done by the body will not be able to be judged except by the body. For God is unjust if someone is not punished or helped through that by which he worked.

If therefore there is any new condition in Christ, the old things have passed; behold, all things have been made new: Isaiah’s prophecy is fulfilled. If he also commands that we cleanse ourselves from the defilement of flesh and blood, it is not that the substance is barred from taking God’s kingdom. If he also destines a holy virgin church to be assigned to Christ, of course as a bride to a bridegroom, an image cannot be joined to an enemy of the thing’s truth. If he also calls false apostles deceitful workers, transformers of himself — of course by hypocrisy — he taxes them as guilty of adulterated way of life, not of adulterated preaching. So far the quarrel was about discipline, not about divinity.

If Satan is transformed into an angel of light, this cannot be aimed at the Creator. For God, not an angel, the Creator would have been said to transform himself into a god of light, not into an angel — if he were not signifying that Satan whom both we and Marcion know as an angel. About paradise he has his own style for every question he suffers. Here I will perhaps wonder at this: if a god of no earthly arrangement could have a paradise of his own — unless he also used the Creator’s paradise by begging, as also the world. And yet to take a man up to heaven is the Creator’s example in Elijah. But I will wonder more that the best god, foreign to striking and raging, applied not even his own but the Creator’s angel of Satan to his apostle for buffetings and, asked by him three times, did not grant it. So Marcion’s god also corrects according to the Creator, rivaling the lofty and putting dynasts down from the throne.

latin: haec enim ad mortis metum et ad ipsius dissolutionis contristationem consolandam retractans etiam per sequentia manifestus, cum subicit ingemere nos de isto tabernaculo corporis terreni. quod de caelo est superinduere cupientes: siquidem et despoliati non inueniemur nudi — id est: recipiemus quod despoliati sumus, id est corpus, et rursus: etenim qui sumus in isto tabernaculo corporis in gemimus, quod grauemur no lentes exui, sed superindui. hic enim expressit quod in prima epistola strinxit: et mortui resurgent incorrupti, qui iam obierunt, et nos mutabimur, qui in carne fuerint reprehensi a deo hic. et illi enim resurgent incorrupti, recepto scilicet corpore et quidem integro, ut ex hoc sint incorrupti, et hi propter temporis ultimum iam momentum et propter merita uexationum antichristi compendium mortis, sed mutati, consequentur, superinduti magis quod de caelo est quam exuti corpus. ita si hi super corpus induent caeleste illud, utique et mortui recipient corpus, super quod et ipsi induant incorruptelam de caelo, quia et de illis ait: necesse est corruptiuum istud induere incorruptelam et mortale istud inmortalitatem. illi induunt, cum receperint corpus, isti superinduunt, quia non amiserint corpus, et ideo (non) temere dixit: nolentes exui corpore, sed superindui, id est nolentes mortem experiri, sed uita praeueniri, uti deuoretur mortale hoc a uita, dum eripitur morti per superindumentum demutationis. ideo quia ostendit hoc melius esse, ne contristemur mortis, si forte, praeuentu, et arrabonem nos spiritus dicit a deo habere, quasi pigneratos in eandem spem superindumenti, et abesse a domino, quamdiu in carne sumus, ac propterea debere boni ducere abesse potius a corpore et esse cum domino, ut et mortem libenter excipiamus. atque adeo omnes ait nos oportere manifestari ante tribunal Christi, ut recipiat unusquisque quae per corpus admisit siue bonum siue malum. si enim tunc retributio meritorum, quomodo iam aliqui cum domino poterunt deputari? et tribunal autem nominando et dispunctionem boni ac mali operis utriusque sententiae iudicem ostendit et corporalem omnium repraesentationem confirmauit. non enim poterit quod corpore admissum est non corpore iudicari. iniquus enim deus. si non per id punitur quis aut iuuatur, per quod operatus est

Si qua ergo conditio noua in Christo, uetera transierunt, ecce noua facta sunt omnia: impleta est Esaiae prophetia. si etiam iubet, ut mundemus nos ab inquinamento carnis et sanguinis, non substantiam *** capere regnum dei. si et uirginem sanctam destinat ecclesiam adsignare Christo, utique ut sponsam sponso, non potest imago coniungi inimico ueritatis rei ipsius. si et pseudoapostolos dicit operarios dolosos transfiguratores sui, per hypocrisin scilicet, conuersationis, non praedicationis adulteratae reos taxat. adeo de disciplina, non de diuinitate dissidebatur.

si satanas transfiguratur in angelum lucis, non potest hoc dirigi in creatorem. deus enim, non angelus, creator in deum lucis. non in angelum, transfigurare se dictus esset. si non eum satanam significaret, quem et nos et Marcion angelum nouimus. (De paradiso suus stilus est ad omnem quam patitur quaestionem. hic illud forte mirabor, si proprium potuit habere paradisum deus nullius terrenae dispositionis; nisi si etiam paradiso creatoris precario usus est, sicut et mundo. et tamen hominem tollere ad caelum creatoris exemplum est in Helia. magis uero mirabor deum optimum, percutiendi et saeuiendi alienum, nec proprium saltem, sed creatoris angelum satanae colaphizando apostolo suo adplicuisse et ter ab eo obsecratum non concessisse. emendat igitur et deus Marcionis secundum creatorem, elatos aemulantem et deponentem scilicet de solio dynastas.

author: Tertullian
english: It will not irk to attend to the shorter letters too. There is savor even in a few. The Jews had killed their prophets. I can say: what is that to the apostle of another god and indeed the best, who is said not even to damn his own people’s faults and who himself somehow kills those same prophets by destroying them? What evil did Israel commit with him if it killed those he also rejected, if he first set a hostile sentence on them? But it offended with their own God: he whose injured party it is will reproach the iniquity — certainly anyone other than the injured one’s adversary. But neither would he have loaded them by charging also the Lord’s killing who killed both the Lord and their prophets — though “their” is the heretic’s addition. For what is so bitter if they destroyed Christ, another god’s preacher, who had butchered their own God’s prophets? But the state of the heightening is that they had killed both the Lord and his servants. Finally if they killed another god’s Christ and another’s prophets, he equalized the impiety, he did not heighten it. But it ought not to have been equalized: therefore it could not be heightened unless committed against the same God under either title. Therefore Christ and the prophets are of the same God.

But what holiness of ours he calls God’s will is to be known from the contraries he forbids — for abstain, he says, from fornication, not from marriage; that each know how to handle his own vessel in honor. How? While not in lust, as the nations. But lust even among the nations is not ascribed to marriage, but to extraordinary and unnatural and monstrous luxuries; and whatever is contrary to shame and uncleanness, which does not shut out marriage but lust, which handles our vessel in marriage’s honor. But I would treat this place with the preference of another, that is fuller, holiness safe, setting continence and virginity before marriages, but not forbidden ones. For I beat back destroyers of the God of marriages, not followers of chastity.

He says those who remain unto Christ’s advent, with those who have died in Christ rising first, will be taken in clouds into the air to meet the Lord. I recognize the heavenly substances themselves — that Jerusalem which is above — already then looking ahead to these and announcing through Isaiah: Who are these that fly here like clouds, like doves with chicks to me? If Christ will prepare this ascent for us, he will be that Christ of whom Hosea: who builds his ascent into the heavens, of course for himself and his. From then from whom shall I hope now, if not from him from whom I heard these things? Which Spirit does he forbid to be quenched, and which prophecies does he forbid to be counted nothing? Of course not the Creator’s Spirit nor the Creator’s prophecies according to Marcion. For what he destroys he himself has already quenched and made nothing, and he cannot forbid what he himself did. Therefore it falls on Marcion to show today in his church from then his God’s Spirit, which is not to be quenched, and prophecies that are not to be counted nothing. And if he has shown what he thinks, let him know we will challenge whatever it is to the form of spiritual and prophetic grace and power, so that it both foretell futures and reveal the heart’s hidden things and expound sacraments. When he has brought out and proved nothing such, we will bring out both the Creator’s Spirit and prophecies preaching according to him. And so it will stand what the apostle spoke of — of those of course that were going to be in the church of that God who, while he is, his Spirit also works and the promise is celebrated. Come now, you who deny the flesh’s salvation and, whenever a body is named first in such a place, interpret it as I know not what other than flesh’s substance: how did the apostle distinguish all substances in us by sure names and set all in one vow of salvation, wishing that our spirit and body and soul be kept without complaint at the advent of our Lord and Savior Christ? For he set both soul and body, as two things as different. For though the soul is also some body of its own quality, as also the spirit, yet when both body and soul are named distinctly, and the soul has its own proper word, not needing the common word body, that is left to flesh, which, not named by its own, must use the common. For I do not see another substance in man after spirit and soul to which the word body is fitted besides flesh — understanding this so often under the name body whenever it is not named; much more here, when what is called body is called by its own name.

Adv. Marc. 5.15: prophetae, corpus, caro, resurrectio.
latin: Breuioribus quoque epistulis non pigebit intendere. est sapor et in paucis. occiderant Iudaei prophetas suos. possum dicere: quid ad apostolum dei alterius et quidem optimi, qui nec suorum delicta damnare dicatur quique et ipse prophetas eosdem destruendo quodammodo perimat? quid mali admisit apud illum Israhel, si occidit quos et ille reprobauit, si prior inimicam in eos sententiam statuit? deliquit autem apud deum ipsorum: is exprobrabit iniquitatem, ad quem pertinet laesus; certe quiuis alius quam aduersarius laesi. sed nec onerasset illos imputando etiam domini necem qui et dominum interfecerunt dicendo et prophetas suos, licet suos adiectio sit haeretici. quid enim tam acerbum, si alterius dei praedicatorem Christum interemerunt qui sui dei prophetas contrucidauerunt? status autem (est) exaggerationis, quod et dominum et famulos eius peremissent. denique si alterius dei Christum alterius prophetas peremerunt, aequauit impietatem, non exaggerauit. aequanda autem non fuit: ergo exaggerari non potuit, nisi in eundem deum commissa ex utroque titulo. ergo eiusdem dei Christus et prophetae.

Quam autem sanctitatem nostram (uoluntatem dei dicat, ex contrariis, quae prohibet, agnoscere est — abstinere enim, inquit, a stupro, non a matrimonio; scire unumquemque uas suum in honore tractare. quomodo? dum non in libidine, qua gentes. libido autem nec apud gentes matrimonio adscribitur, sed extraordinarils et non naturalibus et portentosis luxuriae —: est turpitudini quaque et inmunditiae contraria, quae non matrimonium excludat, sed libidinem, quae uas nostrum in honore matrimonii tractet. hunc autem locum salua alterius, id est plenioris sanctitatis praelatione tractauerim, continentiam et uirginitatem nuptiis anteponens, sed non prohibitis. destructores enim dei nuptiarum, non sectatores castitatis retundo.

Ait eos, qui remaneant in aduentum Christi cum eis, qui mortui in Christo primi resurgent, quod in nubibus auferentur in aerem obuiam domino. agnosco his iam tunc prospectis mirari substantias caelestes ipsam Hierusalem, quae sursum est, et per Esaiam pronuntiare: quinam huc uelut nubes uolant, tamquam columbae cum pullis ad me? hunc ascensum si Christus nobis praeparabit, ille erit Christus, de quo Osee: qui ascensum suum aedificat in caelos, utique sibi et suis. exinde a quo sperabo nunc, nisi a quo haec audiui ? Quem spiritum prohibet extingui et quas prophetias uetat nihil haberi? utique non creatoris spiritum nec creatoris prophetias secundum Marcionem. quae enim destruit, ipse iam extinxit et nihil fecit, nec potest prohibere quae ipse fecit. ergo incumbit Marcioni exhibere hodie apud ecclesiam suam exinde spiritum dei sui, qui non sit extinguendus, et prophetias, quae non sint nihil habendae. et si exhibuit quod putat, sciat nos quodcumque illud ad formam spiritalis et propheticae gratiae atque uirtutis prouocaturos, ut et futura praenuntiet et occulta cordis reuelet et sacramenta edisserat. cum nihil tale protulerit ac probarit, nos proferemus et spiritum et prophetias creatoris secundum ipsum praedicantes. atque ita constabit apostolus de quibus dixerit, de eis scilicet, quae futura erant in ecclesia eius dei, qui dum est, spiritus quoque eius operatur et promissio celebratur. Age nunc, qui salutem carnis abnuitis et, si quando corpus in huiusmodi praenominatur, aliud nescio quid interpretamini illud quam substantiam carnis, quomodo apostolus omnes in nobis substantias certis nominibus distinxit et omnes in uno uoto constituit salutis, optans, ut spiritus noster et corpus et anima sine querela in aduentu domini et salutificatoris nostri Christi conseruentur? nam et animam posuit et corpus, tam duas res quam diuersas. licet enim et anima et] corpus sit aliquod suae qualitatis, sicut et spiritus, cum tamen et corpus et anima distincte nominantur, habet <autem) anima suum uocabulum proprium, non egens communi uocabulo corporis, id relinquitur carni, quae non nominata proprio, communi utatur necesse est. etenim aliam substantiam in homine non uideo post spiritum et animam, cui uocabulum corporis accommodetur praeter carnem, hanc totiens in corporis nomine intellegens, quotiens non nominatur; multo magis hic, cum quae dicitur corpus suo nomine appellatur.

author: Arnobius
english: Do you dare laugh at us when we speak of Gehenna and certain inextinguishable fires into which we have learned souls are cast by their enemies and foes? What of that same Plato of yours, in the volume he composed on the soul’s immortality — does he not name Acheron, Styx, Cocytus, and Pyriphlegethon, in which he asserts souls are rolled, sunk, and burned? And a man of no perverse prudence and of weighed examination and judgment undertakes an insoluble thing: while he says souls are immortal, perpetual, and stripped of bodily solidity, he still says they are punished and afflicted with a sense of pain. Who among men does not see that what is immortal and simple can admit no pain, and that what feels pain cannot have immortality? Yet his authority does not decline far from the truth. For although a gentle man of kindly will believed it inhuman to condemn souls by a capital sentence, he still not absurdly suspected they are cast into rushing rivers foul with balls of flame and muddy gulfs.

For they are cast, and reduced to nothing they vanish in the frustration of perpetual destruction. For they are of mid quality, as has been found with Christ as author, and can perish if they ignore God, and can be freed for life and from ruin if they apply themselves to his threats and indulgences — and what is unknown may lie open.

This is man’s true death, this that leaves nothing remaining — for that which is seen under the eyes is souls’ unyoking from bodies, not the extreme end of abolition — this, I say, is man’s true death, when souls that do not know God are consumed through longest-time torment by fierce fire, into which certain cruelly savage ones, unknown before Christ and exposed by the only one who knows, will cast them.

Adv. Nat. 2.14: gehennae, mediae qualitatis, mors vera.

added_allusions.reason: fear him who can destroy soul; true death beyond body.

latin: 14.1. Audetis ridere nos, cum gehennas dicimus et inextinguibiles quosdam ignes, in quos animas deici ab earum hostibus inimicisque cognovimus? 2. Quid Plato idem vester in eo volumine, quod de animae immortalitate conposuit [Plato, Phaed. 113 d], non Acherontem, non Stygem, non Cocytum fluvios et Pyriphlegethontem nominat, in quibus animas adseverat volvi mergi exuri? Et homo prudentiae non pravae et examinis iudiciique perpensi rem inenodabilem suscipit, ut cum animas dicat immortales perpetuas et ex corporali soliditate privatas, puniri eas dicat tamen et doloris adficiat sensu. 3. Quis autem hominum non videt quod sit immortale, quod simplex, nullum posse dolorem admittere, quod autem sentiat dolorem, immortalitatem habere non posse? Nec tamen eius auctoritas plurimum a veritate declinat. Quamvis enim vir lenis et benivolae voluntatis inhumanum esse crediderit capitali animas sententia condemnare, non est tamen absone suspicatus iaci eas in flumina torrentia. flammarum globis et caenosis voraginibus taetra.

4. Iaciuntur enim et ad nihilum redactae interitionis perpetuae frustratione vanescunt. 5. Sunt enim mediae qualitatis, sicut Christo auctore compertum est, et interire quae possint deum si ignoraverint, vitae et ab exitio liberari, si ad eius se minas atque indulgentias adplicarint, et quod ignotum est pateat.

6. Haec est hominis mors vera, haec nihil residuum faciens - nam illa quae sub oculis cernitur animarum est a corporibus diiugatio, non finis abolitionis extremus - haec inquam est hominis mors vera, cum animae nescientes deum per longissimi temporis cruciatum consumentur igni fero, in quem illas iacient quidam crudeliter saevi et ante Christum incogniti et ab solo sciente detecti.

author: Arnobius
english: “Rather,” he says, “if God is a powerful, merciful keeper, let him turn our minds and make us believe his promises even unwilling.” That, then, is force, not grace, nor the liberality of the leading God, but a childish contest of a mind eager to win. For what is so unjust as to wrench resisting, unwilling wills the other way, to force in what they do not want and what their minds flee, to harm first before you help, and, the earlier state stripped away, to translate them into an alien habit and opinion? You who want to be turned and to suffer force so as to do what you do not want and seize it under compulsion — why do you refuse to take by will what, once turned and changed, you desire to do? “I do not want,” he says, “and I have no will.” Why then do you accuse God as if he fails to bring help to one who desires aid — you who not only scorn and flee his gifts and favors, but also nickname them empty words and chase them with joking jests?

“So unless I become a Christian, I cannot have hope of salvation?” It is so, as you yourself propose. For the parts of giving salvation and of applying to souls what it is fitting and necessary to bestow rest on one alone, enjoined and handed down by God the Father — the remoter and inner causes standing as they do. Just as among you certain gods have certain guardianships, licenses, and powers, and you do not ask of any of them what is not of his power and license, so it is the sole pontificate of Christ to give salvation to souls and to set the spirit of perpetuity upon them. If you believe Father Liber can give a vintage but not medicine, Ceres grain, Aesculapius health, Neptune one thing and Juno another, and Fortune, Mercury, Vulcan each givers of single definite things — then you must also accept this from us: that souls can receive the force of life and safety from no one except from him whom the highest king has set over this gift and office.

This the almighty emperor willed to be the way of salvation, this — so to speak — the door of life; through this alone is the entrance to light, and it is not given otherwise to creep in or break in, all other ways shut and fortified with an impregnable citadel.

Adv. Nat. 2.65: vis/gratia; pontificium Christi; salutis via.
latin: 65.1. ''Immo, inquit, si deus est potens misericors conservator, convertat nobis mentes et invitos faciat suis pollicitationibus credere''. - Vis ergo est ista, non gratia nec dei liberalitas principis, sed ad vincendi studium puerilis atque <vani> animi contentio. 2. Quid est enim tam iniustum, quam repugnantibus, quam invitis extorquere in contrarium voluntates, inculcare quod nolint et quo refugiant animis, prius nocere quam prosis et priore detracto in alienum habitum sententiamque traducere? 3. Tu qui te verti et vim desideras perpeti, ut id quod nolis efficias atque arripias coactus, cur respuis adsumere voluntate id quod versus desideras atque immutatus efficere? ''Nolo, inquit, et voluntatem non habeo''. - Quid ergo criminaris deum tamquam tibi desit opem desideranti ferre? cuius dona et munera non tantum asperneris et fugias, verum inania verba cognomines et iocularibus facetiis prosequaris.

4. ''Christianus ergo ni fuero, spem salutis habere non potero?''. - Ita est, ut ipse proponis. Partes enim salutis dandae conferendi que animis quod tribui convenit necessariumque est adplicari, solus ab deo patre iniunctum habet et traditum, ita se habentibus semotis atque interioribus causis. Ut enim dii certi certas apud vos habent tutelas licentias potestates neque eorum ab aliquo id quod eius non sit potestatis ac licentiae postulatis, ita unius pontificium Christi est dare animis salutem et spiritum perpetuitatis adponere. 5. Si enim patrem creditis Liberum dare posse vindemiam, medicinam non posse, si Cererem fruges, si Aesculapium sanitatem, si Neptunum aliud, aliud posse Iunonem, Fortunam Mercurium Vulcanum rerum esse singulos certarum ac singularum datores: et hoc necesse a nobis est ut debeatis accipere, ab nullo animas posse vim vitae atque incolumitatis accipere nisi ab eo quem rex summus huic muneri officioque praefecit.

6. Hanc omnipotens imperator esse voluit salutis viam, hanc vitae ut ita dixerim ianuam, per hanc solum est ingressus ad lucem neque alias datum est vel inrepere vel invadere ceteris omnibus clausis atque inexpugnabili arce munitis.

author: Arnobius
english: “But the gods are held to be immortal.” Not, then, by nature, but by the will and gift of God the Father. By what pact, then, did he bestow the gift of immortality on gods brought forth under a fixed arrangement, and will he by this pact deign to gift souls with immortality, though savage death seem able to extinguish them and, reduced to nothing, to delete them in irreversible abolition? That divine Plato, sensing many things about God worthy and not common to the crowd, in the discourse and book named Timaeus says gods and the world are of a corruptible nature and not altogether free of dissolution, but by the will of God the king and prince are held in perpetual binding. For what is rightly bound and tied with most perfect knots is kept by God’s goodness; nor can it be loosed by any other than by him who bound it, if the case requires, and gifted by a saving command.

Therefore if the matter is so and it is fitting to judge or believe nothing else, why do you marvel that souls are called by us of mid quality, when Plato says the divinities themselves have mid natures, but continuous and unsetting life is supplied by principal benevolence?

For if perhaps you do not know and it was unknown to you before because of the novelty of the thing, take it late and learn from him who knows and has brought it into the open — Christ: that souls are not daughters of the greatest king nor began to know themselves as generated by him, as is said, and to be proclaimed in the essence of his name, but that they have some other begetter, separated from the emperor by quite many grades of dignity and power, yet noble from his court and by the loftiness of eminent births.

Adv. Nat. 2.36: voluntate/munere; Timaeus bond; Christ revealer.

added_allusions.reason: God alone has immortality; gift vs nature.

latin: 36.1. ''Sed immortales perhibentur dii esse''. - Non ergo natura, sed voluntate dei patris ac munere. Quo igitur pacto immortalitatis largitus est donum dis <die> certa prolatis, et animas hoc pacto dignabitur immortalitate donare, quamvis eas mors saeva posse videatur extinguere et ad nihilum redactas inremeabili abolitione delere. 2. Plato ille divinus multa de deo digna nec communia sentiens multitudini in eo sermone ac libro cui nomen Timaeus scribitur [ Timaeus 41] deos dicit et mundum corruptibilis esse natura neque esse omnino dissolutionis expertes, sed voluntate dei regis ac principis vinctione in perpetua contineri. Quod enim recte sit vinctum et nodis perfectissimis conligatum, dei bonitate servari: neque ullo ab alio nisi ab eo qui vinxit et dissolvi, si res poscat, et salutari iussione donari.

3. Ergo si res est ita nec aliud convenit vel existimare vel credere, quid animas admiramini mediae dici qualitatis a nobis, cum numinibus ipsis dicat Plato medias esse naturas, sed continuam et inocciduam vitam principali benivolentia subrogari?

4. Si enim forte nescitis et antea vobis incognitum propter rei novitatem fuit, accipite sero ac discite ab eo qui novit et protulit in medium Christo, non esse animas regis maximi filias nec ab eo quemadmodum dicitur generatas coepisse se nosse atque in sui nominis essentia praedicari, sed alterum quempiam genitorem his esse, dignitatis et potentiae gradibus satis plurimis ab imperatore diiunctum, eius tamen ex aula et eminentium nobilem sublimitate natalium.

author: Arnobius
english: “But if,” they say, “Christ was sent by God for this — to free unhappy souls from the ruin of destruction — what did the earlier ages deserve, which before his coming were consumed under the condition of mortality?” Can you know what was done with those souls of the most ancient mortals of old — whether help was given them too by some reason, counsel taken and provision made? Can you, I say, know what could be known with Christ teaching: whether ages are infinite or finite from when the human race began to be on earth; when souls were first bound to bodies; who the author of that binding was; rather who the maker of man himself was; where the souls of earlier ones departed; in what parts or regions of the world they were; whether corruptible or the opposite; whether they could have come into the danger of dying unless in the necessary time the savior Christ had met them?

Lay out these worries and leave questions unknown to you: royal pity was imparted to them also, and divine benefits ran equally through all; they were kept, they were freed, and they laid aside mortality’s lot and condition. “By what kind, which, when?” If arrogance, if pride, if elation were absent from you, you could already have known these things from the Author.

Adv. Nat. 2.63: saecula priora; aequaliter beneficia; liberatae.
latin: 63.1. ''Sed si, inquiunt, Christus in hoc missus a Deo est, ut infelices animas ab interitionis exitio liberaret, quid saecula commeruerunt priora, quae ante ipsius adventum mortalitatis condicione consumpta sunt?''. - Potestis enim scire, quid sit cum eis animis actum priscorum veterrimorum que mortalium, subventum et his an sit ratione aliqua, consultum atque provisum? 2. Potestis, inquam, scire id quod Christo potuit docente cognosci, infinita an finita sint saecula ex quo in terris esse genus hominum coepit, quando primum animae corporibus inligatae, quis auctor vinctionis istius, quinimmo ipsius quisnam hominis fabricator, quo priorum abscesserint animae, quibus in mundi partibus aut regionibus fuerint, corruptibiles an contra, potuerintne accedere ad periculum moriendi , nisi tempore necessario conservator occurrisset Christus?

3. Exponite has curas et incognitas vobis relinquite quaestiones: miseratio et illis impertita est regia et aequaliter per omnes divina beneficia cucurrerunt: conservatae sunt, liberatae sunt et mortalitatis sortem condicionem que posuerunt. ''Quo genere, quae, quando?''. - Si adrogantia, si typhus, si elatio abesset a vobis, iamdudum haeG scire <Christo> potuistis auctore.

author: Arnobius
english: “But if souls,” they say, “are mortal and of mid quality, how can they become immortal out of mid qualities?” If we should say we do not know that and have only believed what we heard from one more powerful, where will our credulity seem to have slipped if we believed the omnipotent king that nothing is difficult, nothing hard, if what is impossible for us to do is for him possible and ready at the measure of obedience? For is there anything that can stand against his wills, or what he has willed does not necessarily follow that it comes to be? Or shall we gather from our divisions what can or cannot be done, and not consider that our reasonings are as mortal as we ourselves are and of no name before the prince?

And yet, you who do not believe souls are of mid quality and are held on the mid limit of life and destruction — are not all altogether whom opinion suspects to be gods, angels, demons, or by whatever other name, themselves also of mid quality and wavering in the condition of an ambiguous lot? For if we all concede there is one Father of things, alone immortal and unbegotten, and nothing at all is found before him that was of any name, it follows that all those opinion has believed to be gods of mortals were either generated by him or brought forth at his command. If they are brought forth and generated, they are also of later order and time; if of later order and time, they must have origins and beginnings of birth and life: but what has an entrance and a beginning of starting life necessarily must also have a setting.
