latin: >XLVI. [1] Ecce rursus urgemur etiam de ipsorum somniorum retractatu quibus anima iactatur exprimere. Et quando perueniemus ad mortem? Et hic dixerim: cum deus dederit; nullae longae morae eius quod eueniet. [2] Vana in totum somnia Epicurus iudicauit liberans a negotiis diuinitatem et dissoluens ordinem rerum et in passiuitate omnia spargens, ut euentui exposita et fortuita. Porro si ita est, ergo erit aliquis et ueritatis euentus, quia non capit solam eam euentui omnibus debito eximi. Homerus duas portas diuisit somniis, corneam ueritatis, fallaciae eburneam; respicere est enim, inquiunt, per cornu, ebur autem caecum est. [3] Aristoteles maiorem partem mendacio reputans agnoscit et uerum. Telmessenses nulla somnia euacuant, imbecillitatem coniectationis incusant. Quis autem tam extraneus humanitatis, ut non aliquam aliquando uisionem fidelem senserit? Pauca de insignioribus perstringens Epicuro pudorem imperabo. [4] Astyages Medorum regnator quod filiae Mandanae adhuc uirginis uesicam in diluuionem Asiae fluxisse somnio uiderit, Herodotus refert; item anno post nuptias eius ex isdem locis uitem exortam toti Asiae incubasse. Hoc etiam Charon Lampsacenus Herodoto prior tradit. Qui filium eius tanto operi interpretati sunt, non fefellerunt, siquidem Asiam Cyrus et mersit et pressit. [5] Philippus Macedo nondum pater Olympiadis uxoris naturam obsignasse uiderat anulo: leo erat signum; crediderat praeclusam genituram, opinor, quia leo semel pater est. Aristodemus uel Aristophon coniectans immo nihil uacuum obsignari, filium, et quidem maximi impetus, portendi. Alexandrum qui sciunt, leonem anuli recognoscunt. Ephorus scribit. [6] Sed et Dionysii Siciliae tyrannidem Himeraea quaedam somniauit. Heraclides prodidit. Et Seleuco regnum Asiae Laodice mater nondum eum enixa praeuidit. Euphorion promulgauit. Mithridaten quoque ex somnio Ponti potitum a Strabone cognosco, et Baraliren Illyricum a Molossis usque Macedoniam ex somnio dominatum de Callisthene disco. [7] Nouerunt et Romani ueritatis huiusmodi somnia. Reformatorem imperii, puerulum adhuc et priuatum loci, et Iulium Octauium tantum et sibi ignotum Marcus Tullius iam et Augustum et ciuilium turbinum sepultorem de somnio norat. In Vitelliis commentariis conditum est. [8] Nec haec sola species erit summarum praedicatrix potestatum, sed et periculorum et exitiorum: ut cum Caesar in praelio perduellium Bruti et Cassii Philippis aeger, alias maius tamen discrimen ab hostibus relaturus, de Artorii uisione destituto tabernaculo euadit; ut cum Polycrati Samio filia crucem prospicit de solis unguine et lauacro Iouis. [9] Reuelantur et honores et ingenia per quietem, praestantur et medellae, produntur et furta, conferuntur et thesauri. Ciceronis denique dignitatem paruuli etiamnunc gerula iam sua inspexerat. Cycnus de sinu Socratis demulcens homines discipulus Plato est. Leonymus pyctes ab Achille curatur in somniis. Coronam auream cum ex arce Athenae perdidissent, Sophocles tragicus somniando redinuenit. Neoptolemus tragoedus apud Rhoeteum Troiae sepulcrum Aiacis monitus in somnis ab ipso ruina liberat, et cum lapidum senia deponit, diues inde auro redit. [10] Quanti autem commentatores et affirmatores in hanc rem? Artemon Antiphon Strato Philochorus Epicharmus Serapion Cratippus Dionysius Rhodius Hermippus, tota saeculi litteratura. Solum, si forte, ridebo qui se existimauit persuasurum, quod prior omnibus Saturnus somniarit, nisi si et prior omnibus uixit. Aristoteles, ignosce ridenti. [11] Ceterum Epicharmus etiam summum apicem inter diuinationes somniis extulit cum Philochoro Atheniensi. Nam et oraculis hoc genus stipatus est orbis, ut Amphiarai apud Oropum, Amphilochi apud Mallum, Sarpedonis in Troade, Trophonii in Boeotia, Mopsi in Cilicia, Hermionae in Macedonia, Pasiphaae in Laconica. Cetera cum suis et originibus et ritibus et relatoribus, cum omni deinceps historia somniorum, Hermippus Berytensis quinione uoluminum satiatissime exhibebit. Sed et Stoici deum malunt prouidentissimum humanae institutioni inter cetera praesidia diuinatricum artium et disciplinarum somnia quoque magis indidisse, peculiare solacium naturalis oraculi. [12] Haec quantum ad fidem somniorum a nobis quoque consignandam et aliter interpretandam. Nam de oraculis etiam ceteris, apud quae nemo dormitat, quid aliud pronuntiabimus quam daemonicam esse rationem eorum spirituum qui iam tunc in ipsis hominibus habitauerint uel memorias eorum affectauerint ad omnem malitiae suae scenam, in ista aeque specie diuinitatem mentientes eademque industria etiam per beneficia fallentes medicinarum et admonitionum, praenuntiationum, quo magis laedant iuuando, dum per ea quae iuuant ab inquisitione uerae diuinitatis abducunt ex insinuatione falsae? [13] Et utique non clausa uis est nec sacrariorum circumscribitur terminis; uaga et peruolatica et interim libera est. Quo nemo dubitauerit domus quoque daemoniis patere nec tantum in adytis, sed in cubiculis homines imaginibus circumueniri.

author: Tertullian
english: XLVIII. [1] They affirm that clearer and more cultivated dreams are dreamed toward the outer nights, as if the vigor of souls were already emerging once sleep is drawn out… [2] But I would think these things can be estimated ingeniously rather than proved constantly, even if it is Plato who estimated them; and perhaps they proceed by chance. Otherwise dreams will be from choice if they can be directed. [3] As for distinguishing or withdrawing foods — now presumption, now superstition prescribing a discipline for dreams — it must be examined: superstition, as when a fast is ordered for those about to incubate at oracles to induce chastity; presumption, as when Pythagoreans also for this species spit out the bean as burdensome and inflating fodder. But that threefold brotherhood with Daniel, content with pulse alone lest they be contaminated by the king’s dishes, besides remaining wisdom chiefly redeemed from God the grace of dreams — both of obtaining and of expounding them. [4] … So sobriety will not profit to remove ecstasy, but to commend the ecstasy itself, that it may happen in God. ****** Fast for God, not for dream-tech. Sobriety serves religion so ecstasy is in God — not a pagan incubator’s trick.

added_allusions.reason: pulse; wisdom and dreams from God

latin: >XLVIII. [1] Certiora et colatiora somniari affirmant sub extimis noctibus, quasi iam emergente animarum uigore prodacto sopore. Ex temporibus autem anni uerno magis quieta, quod aestas dissoluat animas et hiems quodammodo obduret et autumnus, temptator alias ualetudinum, succis pomorum uinosissimis diluat. [2] Item ex ipsius quietis situ, si neque resupina neque dextero latere decumbat neque conresupinatis internis, quasi refusis loculis, statio sensuum fluitet aut conpressa iecoris sagina <sedes turbata> sit mentis. Sed haec ingeniose aestimari potius quam constanter probari putem, etsi Plato est qui ea aestimauit; et fortassean casu procedant. Alioquin ex arbitrio erunt somnia, si dirigi poterunt. [3] Nam quod et de cibis distinguendis uel derogandis nunc praesumptio nunc superstitio disciplinam somniis praescribit, examinandum est: superstitio, ut cum apud oracula incubaturis ieiunium indicitur, ut castimoniam inducat, praesumptio, ut cum Pythagorici ob hanc quoque speciem fabam respuunt onerosum et inflatui pabulum. Atquin trina illa cum Daniele fraternitas legumine solo contenti, ne regiis ferculis contaminarentur, praeter sapientiam reliquam somniorum praecipue gratiam a deo redemerunt et impetrandorum et disserendorum. [4] Ieiunus autem nescio an ego solus plurimum ita somniem, ut me somniasse non sentiam. Nihil ergo sobrietas, inquis, ad hanc partem? Immo tanto magis ad hanc, quantum et ad omnem; si et ad superstitionem, multo amplius ad religionem. Sic enim et daemonia expostulant eam a suis somniatoribus ad lenocinium scilicet diuinitatis, quia familiarem dei norunt, quia et Daniel rursus trium hebdomadum statione aruit uictu, sed ut deum inliceret humiliationis officiis, non ut animae somniaturae sensum et sapientiam strueret, quasi non in ecstasi acturae. Ita non ad ecstasin summouendam sobrietas proficiet, sed ad ipsam ecstasin commendandam, ut in deo fiat.

author: Tertullian
english: XLIX. [1] Those who think infants do not dream — since all things of the soul are discharged in life according to the measure of age — let them notice their starts and nods and smiles through rest, so that from the fact they grasp that the motions of a dreaming soul easily break out onto the surface through the tenderness of the flesh. [2] But also that the Libyan nation of Atlantes are said to pass in blind sleep — they are taxed as to the nature of the soul. Further, either Herodotus’s rumor lied sometimes, slanderous against barbarians, or a great force of such demons dominates in that climate… [3] But we also derive dreams from God. Why then would the Atlantes not dream even from God — or because no nation is now foreign to God, the gospel flashing into all the earth and to the ends of the world? So either the rumor lied to Aristotle, or the account is still of demons? Provided that no nature of the soul be believed immune to dreams. ****** No people is outside God’s reach now — and no soul-nature is dream-proof. Gospel light covers the map.
latin: >XLIX. [1] Infantes qui non putant somniare, cum omnia animae pro modo aetatis expungantur in uita, animaduertant succussus et nutus et renidentias eorum per quietem, ut ex re comprehendant motus animae somniantis facile per carnis teneritatem erumpere in superficiem. [2] Sed et quod Libyca gens Atlantes caeco somno transigere dicuntur, animae utique natura taxantur. Porro aut Herodoto fama mentita est nonnunquam in barbaros calumniosa aut magna uis eiusmodi daemonum in illo climate dominatur. Si enim et Aristoteles heroem quendam Sardiniae notat incubatores fani sui uisionibus priuantem, erit et hoc in daemonum libidinibus, tam auferre somnia quam inferre, ut Neronis quoque seri somniatoris et Thrasymedis insigne inde processerit. [3] Sed et a deo deducimus somnia. Quid ergo nec a deo Atlantes somniarent, uel quia nulla iam gens dei extranea est in omnem terram et in terminos orbis euangelio coruscante? Num ergo aut fama mentita est Aristoteli aut daemonum adhuc ratio est? Dum ne animae aliqua natura credatur immunis somniorum.

citation: Commodian — Instructiones 26 (fool, you will not die away from God)
author: Commodian
english: 26. FOOL, YOU WILL NOT DIE AWAY FROM GOD. Fool, you will not die away, nor once dead do you escape your deeds, though you arrange that you feel nothing when dead. You are overcome, senseless one: God the maker of the world lives, whose lawful claims cry out that they hold for the dead. But you, while you rush headlong to live without God, judge the dead extinguished in the fates or credit fate. The eternal God did not arrange it as you think — that the dead are forgetful of what was done before. Now he has made for us unskilled receptacles of death; but after our ashes we shall see those things. Pull yourself out, fool, who think that after funerals you are not. You have made your ruler and lord able to do nothing. But death is not into a void, if you rethink it in the heart. Know what is to be hoped for — for late you will feel him. You were ruler of the flesh; the flesh certainly did not rule you; taken from it, that flesh of yours is stored away. Rightly mortal man is separated from flesh. Therefore mortal eyes will not be able to match it — so our deep has God’s secrets. So give God honor now, fragile one, while you die, and believe that Christ returns you alive from the dead. You ought to render praises to the Almighty in the church. ****** Death is not a blank. God lives; Christ raises; deeds still count.
latin: 26 STULTE NON PERMORERIS DEO. Stulte, non permoreris nec mortuus effugis actus, Tu licet disponas nihil te sentire defuncto. Uinceris, insipiens: uiuit Deus conditor orbis, Legitima cuius clamat ualere defuncto. Tu autem dum praeceps sine Deo uiuere quaeris, Extinctum in fatis iudicas aut fatale credis. Non ita disposuit, ut tu putas, Deus aeternus, Obliuitos esse mortuos de gesto priore. Nunc nobis imperita fecit receptacula mortis, Post cineres autem nostros uidebimus illa. Erue te, stulte, qui putas, post funera non sis. Rectorem dominumque tuum nihil posse fecisti. Mors autem in uacuum non est, si corde retractes. Optandum noscas, nam sero senties illum. Rector eras carnis, non te certe caro regebat; Exemptus ab illa reconditur illa tuorum. Recte mortalis homo separatur a carne. Idcirco nec poterint oculi mortales aequare, Sic habet abyssus noster de Dei secreta. Da nunc ergo Deo, fragilis dum moreris, honorem, Et crede, quod Christus uiuum te de mortuo reddit. Omnipotenti laudes in ecclesia reddere debes.

author: Commodian
english: Who will be able to know properly the one God of the heavens, except the one he has drawn up from wicked error? I was wandering ignorant, roaming, caught by empty hope, while the fury of first age carried me into the air. I was lighter than chaff; as if a hundred heads were on my shoulders, so headlong I was borne wherever. Not content with these things, at last as a criminal Marsian I was almost made by chanting malignant herbs. But thanks to the Lord (and my voice alone is not enough to repay) who at last shone on me, a miserable waverer! And I was handed over, set upon the book of the law, to learn what was there; at once a lamp shone for me. Then truly I recognized God the Lord most high in the heights, and therefore I urge such people to withdraw from error. Who is a better physician than one enlarged by having suffered a wound? Many indeed are brute and unknown, asleep in heart; they set nothing before themselves to know; in beast fashion they seek what they may snatch or whose blood they may live on. While they rejoice to live fattened like pigs, they heap themselves a fine tomb while they clap at riches. The rich will be changed from a poor garment by disgusts. It would suffice them that they eat more readily. If you inquire nothing, that is to be present as beasts. Certainly the most high God set man over the fields — not a wild beast nor a herd animal. Why do we liken ourselves to that? The Almighty wanted man to offer him praises; therefore the divine one himself taught us things to come. Whom that we might believe, he did not only sound by word but also showed mighty deeds when Pharaoh was deceived. ****** God lit the law-lamp for a wanderer. Leave the pig-life; know the one God and praise him.
translator_notes: Source-locked to Latin Carmen (Latin Library HTML).
latin: Quis poterit unum proprie Deum nosse caelorum, Nisi quem is tulerit + ab errore nefando? Errabam ignarus spatians spe captus inani, Dum furor aetatis primae me portabat in auras. Plus eram quam palea leuior; quasi centum inessent In umeris capita, sic praeceps quocumque ferebar. Non satis his rebus, criminosus denique Marsus Paene fui factus herbas incantando malignas. Sed gratias Domino (nec sufficit uox mea tantum Reddere) qui misero uacillanti tandem adluxit! Adgressusque fui traditus in codice legis Quid ibi rescirem; statim mihi lampada fulsit. Tunc uero agnoui Deum <dominum> summum in altis, Et ideo tales hortor ab errore recedant. Quis melior medicus nisi passus uulneris auctus? Multi quidem bruti et ignoti, corde sopiti, Nihil sibi praeponunt cognoscere; more ferino Quaerunt, quod rapiant aut quorum sanguine uiuant. Dummodo laetentur saginati uiuere porci, Ingerunt ut tumulum se pulchrum, dum plaudent diuitiis. <Diuites> mutabuntur <a> paupera ueste fastidiis. Sufficeret illis utique, quod promptius edunt. Si pinguis est opibus, sibi sit, si Caesari dignus: Quid sua praeponunt? fragilis nec respicit ullum. Communicet immo talis bonitatem in omnes Cui Summus diuitias, honores addidit altos. Nec enim uitupero diuitias datas a Summo, Sed culpandus erit, qui superextollitur illis. Suadeo nunc ergo altos sic et humiles omnes, Ut legant assidue uel ista uel cetera legis. Aspice, quam breuis est nobis credita uita Discite, quapropter moriamur nati, prudentes! Quid hebetes morimur, quid profuit lucem uidisse? Si nihil inquiras, hoc est beluarum adesse. Certe Deus summus hominem praeposuit aruis Non feram nec pecudem. Cur nos similemus ad illo Omnipotens uoluit hominem sibi praebere laudes; Idcirco futura docuit nos ipse diuinus. Quem ut crederemus, non tantum uerbo sonauit Sed et demonstrauit fortia Pharaone decepto.

author: Commodian
english: Not this only did he do: under Noah’s times too he showed what he could, since no one was seeking God. Afterward he began to be present more gently little by little, once the flood was done so the earth could be filled. Already almost half of six thousand years was going, and no one knew the Lord, people living every which way. But God, when he saw men’s hearts far too shut, addresses Abraham, whom Moses himself announces. He himself gave the law to the people when Pharaoh was slain, and who he was, the Lord himself foretold from him. Nor content with one prophetic voice does he put himself forward, but he brought many witnesses who cry out about him. This one, then, when you read the proclamations of many seers, you will find has taken flesh for us. Hence now there is wandering — that the Highest ordered such things — and as if … people of stone soften late for gehenna’s fire. We shout into emptiness to the deaf, things to be carried by storms, and we offer light to the blind, supplying it without cause. A soldier stands at the dispatch: one hears, and another shakes it off and does not take the warnings in the heart, but lost he wanders. Who now leaves off — be judges about these! — the one who warns, or the one who will not obey the word? ****** Many prophetic witnesses; the Highest took flesh for us. Hearing and refusing are not the same crime.
translator_notes: Source-locked to Latin Carmen (Latin Library HTML).
latin: Non solum hoc fecit: et Noe sub tempora quoque Ostendit, quae poterat, quoniam Deum nemo quaerebat. Mitior exinde paulatim coepit adesse, Diluuio facto quo posset terra repleri. Iam paene medietas annorum sex milibus ibat, Et nemo scibat Dominum, passimque uiuentes. Sed Deus, ut uidit hominum nimis [ut] pectora clausa, Adloquitur Abraham, quem Moyses enuntiat ipsum. Ipse dedit legem populo Pharaone necato, Et quis esset, Dominus ipse se praedixit ab illo. Nec una contentus prophetica uoce se promit, Sed multos adhibuit testes, qui de illo clamant. Hunc ergo, cum legitis multorum praeconia <uatum>, Inuenietis eum carnem inuenisse pro nobis. Unde nunc erratur, ordinasse talia Summum, Et quasi subsannant, nec sciunt, quod ab ipso ridentur Interdum subicio, qualiter praelegi prophetas, Et rudes edoceo, ubi sit spes uitae ponenda. Quid Deus in primis uel qualiter singula fecit, Iam Moyses edocuit; nos autem de Christo docemus. Non sum ego uates nec doctor iussus ut essem, Sed pando praedicta uatum oberrantibus austris. Ergo mei similes, quos raptim aura deportat, Quaerite iam portum, ubi sunt pericula nulla. Agricola doctus tempestiua longe dinoscit Et, priusquam ueniant, recolligit se<se> sub antra. Estote prudentes, quod imminet ante uidete Et, priusquam ueniant clades, prouidete saluti. Ignauia pueris opus est, non certe robustis: Si decet hoc rudibus, non conuenit aeuo maturis. Quam quidem, pars hominum, non sit moderata uetustas, Sic erit ut perna minime salfacta: putrescat. Nemo petram subigit nisi solus ignis ad escam: Saxei sic homines mollescunt sero gehennae. Clamamus in uacuum surdis referenda procellis Et lumen offerimus caecis sine causa praebentes. Stat miles ad missa<m>: unus audit, et excutit alter Nec accipit corde monita, sed perditus errat. Quis modo relinquit (iudices estote de istis!), Qui monet aut ille, qui non uult dicto parere?

author: Commodian
english: I hope he is not guilty who obeys Caesar’s spoken orders; but the proud opposite destroys his own life. Sometimes what is mine — I who erred before — I show: the right road to you who still wander empty. You, however, choose, pleasing your own judgment: who wants poison, or the sweet cups of life! Good and evil is created in this nature so that after the fates a man may be proven who is worthy of God. Approach already now, whoever you are, to know lasting things: learn who God is, or under whose name he is present! There is God almighty, one, made from his own self, whom below you will find great and himself humble. He was set in the Word, known to himself alone, who is called Father and Son and Holy Spirit. But from when he decided to compose the world with signs… he is immense light alone; where face or eyes or mouth or limbs are noted, thence with his fist to close the circle of the world. Yet when he willed it to be known of himself who he was, from so great a divinity he made himself able to be seen. There are those to whom he appeared in fire, speaking with a voice; he was taken into flesh, whom no region was holding. This is God almighty, Lord of his own making. ****** One almighty God — Word, Father, Son, Spirit — chose to be seen; even taken into flesh.
translator_notes: Source-locked to Latin Carmen (Latin Library HTML).
latin: Spero, reus non est, qui Caesaris dictos obaudit, Contrarius autem perdit sua<m> uita<m> superbus. Interdum quod meum est, qui prius erraui, demonstro Rectum iter uobis, qui adhuc erratis inanes. Uos tamen eligite, arbitrio uestro placentes, Quis uelit uenenum aut suauia pocula uitae! Bonum et malum est in ista natura creatum Ut homo post fata probetur quis Deo dignus. Adgredere iam nunc, quisquis es, perennia nosse: Disce, Deus qui sit uel cuius nomine adsit! Est Deus omnipotens, unus, a semetipso creatus, Quem infra reperies magnum et humilem ipsum. Is erat in uerbo positus, sibi solo notatus, Qui pater et filius dicitur et spiritus sanctus. Sed ex quo decreuit mundum componere signis, Ignem interposuit metuendum angelis ipsis. Quos tamen distribuit minoris potentiae factos, Ut regerent caelos et terram et subdita terrae. Hunc ergo nec ipsi nuntii dinoscere possunt, Qualis sit aut quantus, nisi quod praecepta sequuntur. Est honor absconsus nobis et angelis ipsis, Relucet immensa super caelos et sine fine; Aureum est totum, quod est quasi flammea uirtus. Illic Dei numen est tantum sine cognita forma, Illa sunt secreta solo Deo nota caelorum. Haec gloria Dei est unica super angelos omnes, Hoc Deus est lucis aeternae, hoc spiritus aeui. In primitiua sua qualis sit, a nullo uidetur, Detransfiguratur, sicut uult ostendere sese. Praebet se uisibilem angelis iuxta formam eorum Et homini fit homo, ceterum Deus urbo probat<ur>. Idcirco nec poterit tanti Dei forma dinosci; Quidquid est, unum est, immenso lumine solus; Ubi facies aut oculi aut os aut membra notantur, Inde pugillo suo concludere circulum orbis. At tamen cum uoluit sciri de se ipso qui esset, Numine de tanto fecit se uideri capacem. Sunt quibus in ignem apparuit uoce locutus; Sumptus est in carnem, quem regio nulla capebat. Hic Deus omnipotens, Dominus suae conditionis,

author: Commodian
english: Though he is invisible, he makes himself seen by some. He who is shaped one way now pours himself into the airs; it is not lawful to seek his beginning or end. This God is always without beginning and without end, who, before he made heaven, was borne in the age; whatever heaven holds, he looks out everywhere from heaven and pierces the whole with eyes and hears with ears. So it pleased him that there be a fleshly course of the world, that only everlasting majesty be exalted. For what was before is hard to tell now; though it be written, let us not care for those things. Since we cannot touch all we see, who can know what is beyond Ocean’s bound? We see heaven too, but what is done inside there no one is given to know until the age’s exit. Let it be enough to know the promises about the future; let us stretch to those things eager, devoted with whole mind. As the bird Phoenix plans to be born again from death, it gives us an example that we can rise after funerals; this God almighty most of all urges us to believe: that a time will come for the dead to live again. Though he be dust now, though bones lie stripped, the man is remade as he was who once died, and then the grace of that age will be greater: then there will be no pain or tears in our body; flesh will not take iron, no blister will rise. God will set this up so that there be greater glory for him. He had first made man to be eternal, but that one fell into death when he neglected the commands. For which things God prepared such stories to uncover all the devil’s inventions. God had given that angel as ruler on earth: who, while he envies man, perishes himself first. Meanwhile he sees the just brought through to deeds and keeps wicked Cain for gehenna. The whole human race began to turn in crime, not looking back who their creator was. The high God bore that with indignation and proposed to cast down almost all created things. It is cast down, and Noah is read freed from water. ****** Dust will not have the last word. The invisible God urges phoenix-hope: the dead will live again.
translator_notes: Source-locked to Latin Carmen (Latin Library HTML).
latin: Cum sit inuisibilis, facit se uideri quibusdam. Qui formatur modo, <modo> se diffundit in auras, Cuius nec initium nec finem quaerere fas est. Hic sine initio semper est Deus et sine fine, Qui, prius quam faceret caelum, ferebatur in aeuum; Quidquid tenet caelum, prospicit ubique de caelo Et penetrat totum oculis et auribus audit. Huic ergo placuit carnalem mundi tenorem, Ut exaltaretur sola sempiterna maiestas. Nam, quod erat ante, referre nunc ardua res est; Sit licet descriptum, non sit nobis cura de illis. Cum haec, quae uidemus, non possumus tangere tota, Quis poterit scire, quid sit trans Oceani fine<m>? Et caelum uidemus, sed illic quid intus agatur, Nullo datur scire, donec fiat exitus aeui. Sufficiat tantum de futuro nosse promissa; Ad illa tendamus cupidi, tota mente deuoti. Sicut auis Phoenix meditatur a morte renasci, Dat nobis exemplum, post funera surgere posse; Hoc Deus omnipotens uel maxime credere suadet, Quod ueniet tempus defunctorum uiuere rursum; Sit licet nunc puluis, iaceant licet ossa nudata, Integratur homo, ut fuerat, qui mortuus olim, Et gratia maior tunc erit istius aeui, Non dolor nec lacrimae tunc erunt in corpore nostro, Non caro recipiet ferrum, non pustula surget. Hoc Deus instituet, ut sit illi gloria maior. Hic fecerat primum hominem, ut esset aeternus, Sed ruit in mortem neglectis ille praeceptis. Propter quae storias tantas Deus esse parauit Ut inuentiones diabuli detegeret omnes. Rectorem in terra dederat Deus angelum istum: Qui, dum inuidetur homini, perit ipse priorque. Interea iustos per ipsos cernit ad actos Et facinerosa Cain [in] gehenna reseruat. In scelere coepit uersari gens omnis humana, Nec respicientes, quis esset creator eorum. Quod Deus excelsus indigne pertulit illud, Deicere proposuit uniuersa paene creata. Deicitur et legitur Noe liberatus ab aqua,

author: Commodian
english: The rest perished in the flood by heavenly wrath. From here, as at the start, the earth is filled little by little. The earlier crime yielded, but another disaster stuck. Fools set out to build a tower under the stars so that as if by it they could climb the heavens. When God saw it done under one speech he came down and made them speak with diverse tongue. From there he scattered them through remote islands of earth so they became nations speaking with varied talk. Then the unteachable race lived a life of wildness; no one knew God, no one argued about life. For that rash one had crept into the raw through the waters of the soul, warped bitter minds, and by deceit persuaded them to love unspeakable couplings, to live by plunder in joy with blood poured out. Fools chase this glory for a short time; by which no pardon frees them saying they were seduced. If an adulterer urges, the fault is yours to follow such a one; he does not damn you — you damn yourself of your own will. The untaught wandered by the old enemy’s cheat, forgetful of the Lord, following malign works. Lest such robbery of the bandit go on long, when the time was portioned he at last took pity once it was taken away. It pleased him to speak with one of many, to make a people beloved by crossing over to him. From then the profane began that there is one God and to become a people according to God’s decrees. For Rebecca had distinguished two peoples from herself: this one was made first so that the other might succeed him. In Egypt first the foster-child grew in Israel; from there God cast them out with Moses as leader, through whom he himself gave them the law on Mount Sinai, so that our posterity might know the one Lord. Then he ordered prophets from them to say that God is held cheap by them in a man. The Lord had led them into the promised land so they would live there under the law until he himself came. The nation ungrateful for goods refused to bear the yoke of commands, but rather flowered turned back in the old crime; nor did it ever stop: today too it is held such. ****** Two peoples from Rebecca; one Lord on Sinai. Following the seducer is your own damnation — not his.
translator_notes: Source-locked to Latin Carmen (Latin Library HTML).
latin: Ceteri diluuio perierunt ira caelesti. Hinc, sicut initio, paulatim terra repletur. Cessit prius facinus, sed alter<a> clades adhaesit. Adgressi sunt stulti turrem fabricare sub astris Ut quasi per illam possent ascendere caelos. Quod Deus ut uidit fieri sub una loquella Descendit et fecit, loquerentur lingua diuersa. Quos inde disparsit per insulas terrae semotos, Ut fierent gentes uario sermone loquentes. Tunc genus indocile uitam feritatis agebat; Nemo Deum sciebat, disputabat nemo de uita. Irrepserat quoniam rudibus temerarius ille Per latices animae, deprauauit mentes acerbas Persuasitque dolo coitus infandos amare, Uiuere rapinis in gaudio sanguine fuso. Hanc gloriam stulti prosequuntur tempore paruo; Quo nulla uenia liberat se dicendo seductos. Si suadet adulter, culpa est tua prosequi talem; Non ille te damnat, sed tu tua sponte te damnas. Errabant indocti ueteris fallacia hostis, Obliti Dominum, opera maligna sequentes. Quod, diu ne fieret grassatio tanta latronis, Tempore partito miseratus est tandem ablato. Complacuit illi colloqui cum uno de multis, Ut faceret populum ad se transeundo dilectum. Ex eo ceperunt unum Deum esse profani Et fieri populus secundum Dei decreta. Duos enim populos distinxerat ex se Rebecca: Hic prior est factus, alter ut succederet illi. In Aegypto primum in Israhel concreuit alumnus; Inde Deus illos eiecit duce Moyse, Per quem dedit illis <ipse> legem in monte Sina, Ut nostra posteritas Dominum cognosceret unum. Deinde prophetas ex ipsis dicere iussit, Quod Deus in hominem depretiatur ab illis. Induxerat eos Dominus in terra promissa, Ut ibi sub lege uiuerent, donec ipse ueniret. Gens ingrata bonis noluit iugum ferre praeceptis, Sed magis in scelere prisco reuoluta florebat; Nec umquam desinuit: hodie quoque talis habetur;

author: Commodian
english: God left aside, it prefers the age’s luxuries. This the Lord most of all drives his beloved to avoid; he forewarns them to be cut off wholly from the age. If he called them sons, let us stay in his holy things; why do we go outside following adulterous shows? The ancient seducer deceives all through such things: he sends luxuries by which he may ruin the High One’s sons — agony to be sent, going to bloody shows or too obscene ones, for the chaste to know the unchaste. If one had been chaste, unchaste he advances from there, and pleasing, smiling, whom then evil joys tempt. In these luxuries the first people lived and always withdrew unarmed from God’s law. To cleanse them God often sent foster-sons to correct them again when warped from the Highest. They never wanted to take divine words but by their own will always raged, unfit. They slaughtered the just who rebuked them wrongly while they refused to take heaven’s discipline bit. They saw Isaiah; they stone Jeremiah standing up; they behead John; they cut Zechariah’s throat at the altars. And he himself came who had been foretold by them, and he suffers as he willed under our likeness. In whose exit every prophecy was filled. Daniel had said this one was latest to the prophets. He was the one for whom the seers sang from the trumpet, about to come into his own, whom his own would deny. Always unforeseen and stiff-necked kickers, while they spit the form they lose the law’s sacraments. Neither justice nor humble flesh born broke them, nor such goodness or care of the sick from the word. O dutiful religion, O majesty so to be revered, whose medicine so advanced on earth! He cut no one with iron, healed with no plaster, but without torment at once by his own word he healed. Seeing such things the Jews were troubled in mind, who rather were led by envy into jealousy’s zeal, not looking back at the buried prophets’ sayings — that such a man would come who would scatter them. Until the Lord came, the prophets were singing. ****** Cut off from the age’s shows. The foretold One heals by word — and fills every prophecy in his suffering.

latin: Praetermisso Deo luxuria<s> saeculi mauult. Quod maxime Dominus cogit euitare dilectos; Abscisos in totum a saeculo praemonet esse. Si filios dixit, in illius sancta moremur; Quid foris egredimur adulteri pompa<s> sequentes? Seductor antiquus per talia decipit omnes: Immittit luxurias, per quas perdat filios Alti Agonia mitti, spe<cta>culis ire cruentis Aut nimis obscenis, impudica nosse pudicis. Si fuerat castus, incestus proficit inde Et placens adridens, quem tunc mala gaudia temptant. In istis luxuriis populus primitiuus agebat Et a lege Dei semper recedebat inermis. Ad quos emundandos saepe Deus misit alumnos Ut illos corrig<er>ent deprauatos denuo Summo. Excipere numquam uoluerunt dicta diuina Sed uoluntate sua saeuierunt semper inepti. Mactabant iustos redarguentes illos inique Dum nollent accipere frenum disciplinae caelestis. Esaiam serrant, lapidant Hieremiam erecti, Iohannem decollant, iugulant Zachariam ad aras. Et uenit et ipse, fuerat qui praedictus ab illis, Et patitur, quomodo uoluit, sub imagine nostra. Cuius in exitio omnis prophetia repleta est. Dixerat hunc Daniel nouissimum esse prophetis. Is erat, quem propter uates de tuba canebant, In sua uenturum propria, quem sui negarent. Improuidi semper et dura ceruice recalces, Dum respuunt forma<m>, sacramenta legis amittunt. Non illos iustitia, humilis non caro nata refregit, Nec bonitas tanta aut aegrorum cura de uerbo. O pia religio, o tam ueneranda maiestas, Cuius medicina taliter in terra profecit! Non ullum de ferro secuit, non emplastro curauit, Sed sine tormento statim suo dicto sanauit. Talia uidentes turbabant<ur> mente Iudaei, Qui magis inuidia ducti sunt in zelo liuoris, Non respicientes prophetarum dicta sepulti, Quod ueniret homo talis, qui dispergeret illos. Quousque ueniret Dominus, prophetae caneba<n>t:

author: Commodian
english: From when he came, prophecy fell silent for the Jews. After him they came into exile with hardened heart and do not yet discern why they have suffered such things. It had been foretold them by Isaiah the prophet and likewise by Daniel to lose the land; yet not before, unless the leader of the city in it should hang on the wood, and then it become desert. Suddenly what glory shone on a nation, that a people should become a people that was not before! Was Esau beloved by the father not stunned that the younger brother would take the first things? So neither could the synagogue know the time when and under what leader it would fall from its private right; as it was written, that birds know their times, but this people did not understand that I was present. It came that the ruler of heaven himself should come: according to the scriptures he was not counted by them. The Lord had been foreknowing this, as one who knows all things; therefore through the prophets’ mouths he foretold these things. A people too stiff-necked and always rebelling — while it claimed first place for itself, the case was cut off. Into their courses he set gentiles in charge; he had said this before: Nations will hope in him. For the stone itself was set into Zion’s foundations — whoever believed in it would have eternal life. Daniel marks this Holy of Holies to be anointed and after him the royal chrism to be wiped out. David said that: to be fixed with a nail, silent — They dug, he says, my hands and my feet themselves. Solomon too prophesies of him so openly, that the Jews would say, Let us kill the just one! Jeremiah likewise shows the cross in figure: Come, let us cast wood into his bread! saying. But their leader Moses heralds to them: Before your eyes life will hang slain. Here the Father came in the Son, one God everywhere: nor was he called Father unless the Son had been made. For he did not leave heaven to give birth on earth, but, as he arranged, majesty was seen on earth — from his own power he made himself be born in flesh. ****** Prophets fall silent when he comes. Wood, nail, stone of Zion: the Father in the Son, one God, majesty in flesh.

latin: Ex eo, quo uenit, tacuit prophetia Iudaeis. Post quem in exilium deuenerunt corde durato Nec modo dinoscunt, quapropter sint talia passi. Praedictum fuerat illis ab Esaia propheta Et Danihelo similiter perdere terram; Quam non ante tamen, nisi dux ciuitatis in ipsa Penderet in ligno, fieret deserta deinde. Desubito qualis obfulsit gloria genti, Ut fieret populus, populus qui non erat ante! Non fuit adtonitus Esau dilectus a patre, Iunior quod frater primitiua toll<er>et ille? Sic nec sinagoga potuit cognoscere tempus, Quando et quo duce caderet de suo priuato; Sicut erat scriptum, quod auis sua tempora norunt, Nam populus iste non me intellexit adesse. Uentum est, ut ipse dominator caeli ueniret: Secundum scripturas non est computatus ab ipsis. Praescius hoc fuerat Dominus, quasi cuncta qui nouit; Idcirco per ora prophetarum ista praedixit. Gens ceruicosa nimis semperque rebellans Dum sibi primatum uindicaret, causa resecta est. In quorum stadia gentiles esse praefecit; Dixerat hoc ante: Gentes sperabunt in ipsum. Nam lapis immissus ipse est in fundamenta Sion Crederet in quo quis, haberet uitam aeternam. Hunc sanctum sanctorum Daniel perungii designat Et exterminari post illum chrisma regale. Dauid illud dixit, clauis configi silentem: Effoderunt, inquit, manus meas et pedes ipsi. Salomon quoque tam aperte de illo prophetat, Occidamus iustum! dicturos esse Iudaeos. Hieremias totidem crucem figurate demonstrat: Uenite, mittamus lignum in pane! dicentes. Dux autem ipsorum Moyses praeconiat illis: Ante tuos oculos pendebit uita necata. Hic pater in filio uenit, Deus unus ubique: Nec pater est dictus, nisi factus filius esset. Nec enim reliquit caelum, ut in terra pareret, Sed, sicut disposuit, uisa est in terra maiestas De uirtute sua carna<liter na>sci <se fecit>

author: Commodian
english: …one may make a single fringe. Already flesh was God, in which God’s power was at work. What of this — that the prophets sing the invisible is to be seen, so that such brightness should also become man for us? Nor would our people have sprung forth in the new law if the Almighty had not ordered it beforehand concerning us. This was the Almighty, in whose name the nations were wholly to believe, as the prophet Isaiah said: A man will rise in Israel from Jesse’s root; the nations will hope in him, by whose sign they are kept. And another said he is a witness through the world — that he himself, a prince, be shown to the nations. In the psalms it is sung: The Lord has reigned from the wood; let the earth exult, let many islands be glad. So too patriarch Jacob: a true blessing appeared among the nations; this will be the hope of the nations, he says. Under heaven no other name is set forward except Christ’s, in whose name the nations everywhere have believed. We are not so urged to believe for a time of suffering, but for a future time, living in the eternal. This hope is to be hoped by us — to enjoy everlasting hope — not those joys our fragile state soon changes. Though riches be before the eyes richly to be enjoyed, you are shut out from them, a frail death put in their place; or if you last, you yourself shudder while living; or if health is bad, what is life to you? The whole in which we live under this age is torment; hence indeed hope in the future must be sought for us: this God urges, this the law, this Christ’s passion — that we believe we will rise in a new age. So God’s law cries: when the High One became humble, hell would yield, so that Adam be raised from death. The Lord went down into the tomb, pitying his own fashioned clay, and so through hidden things he emptied death’s strong things. The Lord crept on the old robber, hidden, and willed to suffer so that he might more throw him down. That one indeed bold and always savage as an enemy, while he hopes to rage against a man, was beaten by the Highest. Through what the malign one had first thrown man down to death — ****** Flesh was already God at work. Nations hope in Jesse’s root; the Lord reigns from the wood; he enters the tomb to empty death.

latin: ............................................. ........... licet facere fimbriam unam. Iam caro <Deu>s erat, in qua Dei uirtus agebat. Quid, quod prophetae canunt, inuisibilem esse uidendum, Ut claritas tanta fieret homo quoque pro nobis. Nec populus noster prosilisset in noua lege, Si non Omnipotens ordinasset ante de nobis. Hic erat Omnipotens, cuius <in> nomine gentes Credere omnino, quod propheta dixit Esaias: Exurget in Israel homo de radice Iesse In illum sperabunt gentes, cuius signo tuentur. Et alter dixit testem illum esse per orbem Manifestari eum principem nationibus ipsum. In psalmis canitur: Dominus regnauit a ligno; Exultet terra, iocundentur insulae multae. Sic et patriarcha Iacob: benedictio uera Paruit in gentes; hic erit spes gentium, inquit. Sub caelo non aliud nomen est nisi Christi praelatum, In cuius nomine crediderunt gentes ubique. Non ita suademur credere pro tempore passo Sed propter futurum tempus in aeterno uiuentes. Haec speranda nobis spes est sempiterno frunisci Non ista, quae fragili<s> cito mutat gaudia nostra. Sint licet diuitiae prae oculis laute fruendae Excluderis illis substituta morte caduca; Aut si perseuera[ue]ris, horrescis ipse uiuendo Aut si ualetudo fuerit mala, quo tibi uita? Tormentum est totum, quo uiuimus isto sub aeuo; Hinc adeo nobis est spes in futuro quaerenda: Hoc Deus hortatur, hoc lex, hoc passio Christi, Ut resurrecturos nos credamus in nouo saeclo. Sic Dei lex clamat: fieret cum humilis Altus, Cederet infernus, ut Adam leuaretur a morte Discendit in tumulum Dominus suae plasmae misertus Et sic per occulta inaniuit fortia mortis. Obrepsit Dominus ueteri latroni celatus Et pati se uoluit, quo magis prosterneret ipsum. Ille quidem audax et semper saeuus ut hostis, Dum sperat in hominem saeuire, uictus a Summo est. Per quod prius hominem prostrauerat morti malignus,

author: Commodian
english: From that very thing he was beaten; from where life comes forth for us. Adam, having tasted the fruit, went away ordered to die; from whose sin we likewise all die the same. But again the Lord said: From the living tree if he takes, let him live forever upright. Death was in a tree and in a tree life was hiding, where God the Lord hung, finder of our life. This tree of life the Lord had foretold to be, so that whoever believes him may be as if he takes from there. He also takes and tastes sweetly the precepts of the most high God and departs from death, because he rises the stronger. Whoever believes in Christ tastes of the tree of life, where the Lord was hung, foretold to Moses. Isaiah announces this one himself to be humble and exceedingly cast down, as if a servant’s figure: And we saw him, and he was not of shining form, a man set under blow, knowing how to bear all things. He grieves for us and carries our sins, and for our crime God handed him over. Who, when he was harassed, was silent like a lamb at the altars. This was already not a mere man, but God was flesh for us; which plainly appears — this was God’s name arising, which now is held a shining name among the nations. This Malachi the prophet sings, who is also himself a messenger, when he also rejects the Jews’ sacrifices saying: Your sacrifice will not be accepted by me, but in every place the nations offer to my name, among whom my excellent name is magnified, who without blood offer to my name cleanly. For he himself was humble, hiding under a great name, who from himself through prophetic mouths cries: I am not stubborn, he says, nor do I contradict the one who harms; my back too I set for scourges to be struck, and my jaws for unjust palms to strike; I offered them and did not turn my face from their spits. Folly came over many, that God suffered such things, so that the crucified be declared founder of the world. So it pleased him (using no one’s counsel, nor could another) to come for us in such a way. The enemy, when envious, invented death — ****** Tree killed; tree hides life. Believe, and you taste that wood. The Servant-God in flesh; nations offer without blood.

latin: Ex ipso deuictus; unde nobis uita prouenit. Adam degustato pomo mori iussus abiit; Cuius de peccato morimur sic et omnis idemque. Sed iterum dixit Dominus: De ligno uitali Si sumpserit ille, in aeternum uiuat honestus. Mors in ligno fuit et ligno uita latebat, Quo Deus pependit Dominus, uitae nostrae repertor. Hoc lignum uitae Dominus praedixerat esse, Ut, qui credet ei, sic sit quasi sumat abinde. Et sumit et gustat suauiter Dei summi praecepta Et discedit, quoniam potior resurgit, a morte. Qui credit in Christo, de ligno uitae degustat, Quo fuit suspensus Dominus Moysi praedicto. Hunc ipsum Esaias humilem denuntiat esse Et nimis deiectum, fuerit quasi serui figura: Et uidimus illum, nec erat praeclarae figurae, In plaga depositus homo, sciens omnia ferre. Hic dolet pro nobis et peccata nostra reportat, Et pro facinore nostro Deus tradidit illum. Qui, cum uexaretur, tacuit sicut agnus ad aras. Hic homo iam non erat, sed erat Deus caro pro nobis; Quod palam apparet, hoc erat Dei nomen oriri, Quod modo praeclarum nomen apud gentes habetur. Hoc Malachiel canit propheta, qui et angelus ipse, Cum et Iudaeorum reprobet sacrificia dicens: Non erit acceptum mihi sacrificium uestrum, Sed in omni loco offerunt meo nomini gentes, Apud quos eximium nomen meum magnificatur, Qui sine cruore offerunt meo nomini munde. Nam fuit is ipse humilis latens nomine magno, Qui de semet ipso per ora prophetica clamat: Contumax non sum, ait, neque contradico nocenti, Dorsum quoque meum posui ad flagella caedendum Maxillasque meas palmis feriendas iniquis Praebui nec faciem auerti sputis eorum. Stultitia subiit multis, Deum talia passum, Ut enuntietur crucifixus conditor orbis. Sic illi complacuit (consilium neminis usus, Nec alius poterat) taliter uenire pro nobis. Mortem adinuenit, cum esset inuidus, hostis,

author: Commodian
english: Which death the Lord drank, having suffered, rising from hell. Therefore he also did not will to show plainly what he was, but said he was a Son sent by the Father. So he himself had handed himself over to be called by the prophets, that God on earth should be the Son of the Most High. This he himself also utters, when he was humble in flesh, and witnesses to the Father, to confirm prophetic mouths. From Israel we read such a man rises, and he is a man, he says, and who knew him among them? Jeremiah says. This is our God, equal; after these things he was also seen on earth and lived among humans. But Isaiah: You are God, and we did not know; and God is in you, and besides you no other is held. And who would come at the prophets’ setting by the law? Sing to the Lord, the name is God to him who comes! And the forty-fourth psalm says of him: I will be exalted among the nations with a great name. And elsewhere we read: Today I have begotten you, son; Ask, and I will give you, and you will have nations as heirs. Certainly it already appears who God is and who is in him, and in whose name we nations everywhere should believe: It was said to my Christ, whose right hand I hold — let the nations hear, and let him rule the nations. What need of more, when the matter is so openly proven, when that people which is taxed already rejoices in him? But those miserable ones who dress up empty tales and smear him as a magician would have shut their beaks when the singers sang. What shall I call them, before they had been scattered — whom not even exile’s necessity itself broke? If a magician had been present, why then were the prophets singing one to come from heaven, that he himself be the hope of the nations? If they announce falsely of themselves that they lose the land — which came about from them — so will things about him also be false. But because they are always spurned, since they were bloody, they rebel against their own Lord by calling him a magician. They also refuse to hear what the seers said against them — that they would not understand wholly under that very end. God himself described them: With shut breast let them not see with eyes nor understand with hardened heart; for he thickened the heart of this unjust people. ****** He drank death and rose. Son sent by the Father — our God seen on earth. Smearing ‘magician’ is shut-heart rebellion, not exegesis.

latin: Quam ebibit Dominus passus ex inferno resurgens. Idcirco nec uoluit se manifestare, quid esset, Sed filium dixit se missum fuisse a patre. Sic ipse tradiderat semet ipsum dici prophetis, Ut Deus in terris Altissimi filius esset. Hoc et ipse fremit, humilis in carne cum esset, Testaturque patrem, ut ora prophetica firmet. Ex Israel legimus hominem resurgere talem Et homo est, inquit, et quis eum nouit in ipsis? Hieremias ait. Hic Deus est noster aequalis Post haec et in terris uisus est conuersatus humanis. Esaias autem: Tu es Deus, et nesciebamus: Et Deus in te est, et praeter te non alter habetur. Et quis in occansum prophetarum lege ueniret? Cantate Domino, nomen est Deus illi, qui uenit! Et psalmus de ipso quartus quadragesimus inquit: Exaltabor ego in gentibus nomine magno. Et alibi legimus: Hodie te genui, fili; Pete, et dabo tibi, et habebis gentes heredes. Certe iam apparet, qui sit Deus et quis in ipso, Et cuius in nomine crederemus gentes ubique: Dictum est Christo meo, teneo cuius dexteram, illud: Exaudiant gentes, et imperet gentibus ipse. Quid plurimis opus est, cum res tam aperte probatur, Cum is, qui taxatur, populus iam in illo laetatur? Illi autem miseri, qui fabulas uanas adornant Et magum infamant, canentibus rostra clusissent. Quales eos dicam, antequam dispersi fuissent, Quos nec exulatus fregit necessitas ipsa? Si magus adfuerat, cur ergo prophetae canebant Uenturum e caelo, ut esset spes gentium ipse? Si false de ipsis pronuntiant perdere terram, Quod prouenit de eis, sic eri<n>t et falsa de illo. Sed quia sunt spreti semper quod cruenti fuerunt, Contra suum Dominum rebellant dicere magum. Nec uolunt audire, quae dixerunt uates in illos, Quod non intellegerent in totum fine sub ipsa. Ipse Deus illos descripsit: Pectore clauso Nec uideant oculis nec intellegant corde durato; Incrassauit enim cor populi huius iniqui,

author: Commodian
english: So that they recognize nothing until they are healed by my word. God was foretold to be born in flesh for us, so that their torment should become the greater by desert: Behold, God himself will give you a sign from on high: A virgin will conceive and the earth will bear the heavenly one; and he will be called Emmanuel, he had commanded them — which the Latin tongue unfolds as ‘God with us.’ Hear that he himself would be nursed with honey and butter, and the word: he would take Samaria before he spoke. But this is a closed history, which the learned unroll, that a nursing child without battle would enter on spoils; whose passion was foretold beforehand in such a way that God should become passible with blood poured out. Isaiah says: Like a sheep led to the altar, and he did not cry with a voice; he bore all things patiently. He is fixed with nails, which David had once foretold; and they gave him vinegar to drink according to the scriptures. And: for my garments, he said, they cast a lot — which was done, and we read all things carried out in him. Darkness too was made for three hours from the sixth, and the day hurried to bring on night’s stars. This had been foretold to happen through the prophet Amos, that it should suddenly cover itself through the holy solemnities. O evil offspring, O people with a sly face! I begot children, said God, who would deny me. And he said: Hear the trumpet’s voice. We will not, they say. This Ezekiel says: Therefore the nations will hear from afar. In one heading I want to touch the book Deuteronomy: You will be at the head, nations; for the unbelieving behind. If the rebels surely spit back all the things said above — know what they oppose, when the matter is spoken so openly? See already therefore, you doubtful who have floated until now, that the nations were prior in the Lord in scripture. Now therefore it is right to believe the one the books mark, not empty idols who are cultivated in vain for life, nor to be joined to those pleasure-led and without rein, who love luxuries more than the Highest’s precepts. One fault is not enough for those who refuse to believe — they even smear: We cast him into a pit. Wherefore the Lord too, indignant, disputes them: ****** Emmanuel, nails, vinegar, lots, noon-dark: the books mark him. Nations were already prior in the Lord — leave the pit-smear and the idols.

latin: Ut nihil agnoscant, donec meo uerbo sanescant. Praedictus est Deus carnaliter nasci pro nobis, Ut fieret illis merito cruciatio maior: Ecce dabit Deus ipse uobis signum ab alto: Concipiet uirgo et pariet terra caelestem; Emmanuel autem uocetur, iusserat illos; Quod lingua Latina 'Deus nobiscum' euoluit. Audite, quod ipse nutriretur melle, buturo, Et uerbum: Samari<m> caperet priusquam loqueretur. Sed haec est historia clausa, de qua docti reuoluunt, Ut paruulus lactans sine pugna praedas iniret; Passio cuius praedicta est taliter ante, Ut Deus passibilis fieret profuso cruore. Esaias ait: Tamquam ouis ductus ad aram, Nec uoce clamauit, patienter omnia gessit. Suffigitur clauis, quod Dauid praedixerat olim; Quem et potauerunt secundum scripturas acetum. Et: in uestimentis meis, dixit, sortemque miserunt, Quod factum, et legimus in illo omnia gesta. Fuerunt et tenebrae factae tribus horis a sexta Festinauitque dies inducere sidera noctis. Praedictum hoc fuerat fieri per prophetam Amos, Ut tegeret subito sese per sollemnia sancta. O mala progenies, <o popule> subdola fronte! Generaui suboles, dixit Deus, qui me negarent. Et dixit: Audite uocem tubae. Nolumus, aiunt. Hoc dicit Ezechiel: Audient ergo gentes a longe. Uno uolo titulo tangere librum Deuteronomium: In caput eritis, gentes; nam increduli retro. Si respuunt certe omnia supra dicta rebelles S<c>ite quid opponunt, cum res tam aperte dicatur? Uidete iam ergo, dubii qui nunc usque natati Quod gentes in Domino fuerint scriptura priores. Nunc ergo fas est credere, quem libri designant, Non idolis uanis, qui frustra pro uita coluntur Nec istis adiungi uoluptuosis et sine freno, Qui magis luxurias diligunt quam Summi praecepta. Non est culpa satis una, qui credere nolunt, Sed magis infamant: In puteum misimus illum. Quapropter et Dominus indignatus iurgiat illos:

author: Commodian
english: For your sake my name is blasphemed among the nations, he says. If he was thrown into a pit, why then is it cried that he rises? From the depths, Lord, you set my soul in place: I slept, he says, and took sleep secure; by the Lord’s help I rose, having suffered no evil. And again he says: You will not abandon into hell, nor will you give your holy one to see decay too. Here sounding he says: Son of the prophet, I ascend, that I may say the Lord Most High suffered through misery. And in the book of psalms it is cried about the Lord’s death — not as they think David reports about himself. Or if they think that, do all things he said fit? David was not scourged nor lifted on a cross. What? Jews prophesy in Saturn’s manner; they gather into fables when it is already turning on them. Let them not slap as witchcraft one lifted on a cross. For the unknowing, untaught, ignorant they invent such things. Who is that God whom we fixed on a cross? they say, unwilling to look at the scriptures, blinded in heart. Behold another prophet sings, repeating again, by whose voice nonetheless such an edict is titled: Now I will rise, says the Lord; now I will be glorified — ****** Pit-smear dies when resurrection is cried. Psalms of the Lord’s death are not David’s private scourging story.

latin: Propter uos nomen meum blasphematur in gentibus, inquit. Si missum in puteum, sed resurgere quare clamatur? Ab inferis, Domine, animam meam imposuisti: Ego dormiui, ait, et somnum cepi securus Auxilio Domini surrexi, nihil mali passus. Et iterum dicit: In infernum non derelinques Nec dabis sanctum tuum interitum quoque uidere. Hic personans ait: Fili prophetae, ascendo, Ut Dominum dicam passum per miseria<m> summum. Et in libro psalmorum de Domini morte clamatur, Non ut illi putant Dauid de ipso referre. Aut si putant illud, congruit uniuersa, quae dixit? Non est flagellatus Dauid nec cruce leuatus. Quid? Uaticinantur Iudaei more Saturni, In fabulas coeunt, cum iam declinetur in illos. Non quasi maleficium alapantur cruce leuatum. Insciis, indoctis, ignorantibus talia fingunt. Quis Deus est ille, quem nos cruce fiximus? aiunt Nolentes respicere scripturas, corde caecati. Ecce canit alius repetens iterumque propheta, Cuius uoce tamen titulatur talis edictus: Nunc exurgam, ait Dominus, nunc clarificabor,

author: Commodian
english: Now you understand; now your confusion will be: You think empty things, therefore fire will hold you. These Isaiah says. Then so also majesty itself, when it was in flesh, professes who he was: No one trying could take my soul away, but I of my own will lay it down from myself by my decree. And I have power to take it again upon it. More openly still it is cried about the just one’s death, so that it may appear the more that the Jews were hardened: Behold the just perishes, and indeed no one understands; but the beloved’s burial will be into peace. Why do they smear that he was sent down into a pit, when we read that he was handed over to burial? Shameful, cruel, blind, proud — who ought rather to mourn from the deed, they applaud! For Solomon, inspired, prophesies about him and presses more fully to show the just one: he recounts how their own malice taught them to rage. See — they themselves are blind and say others are. Solomon said to them: They did not know God’s secrets. ****** He lays life down and takes it again. The just one’s tomb is peace — not your pit-story. Solomon: you never knew God’s secrets.

latin: Nunc intellegitis, nunc erit confusio uestra: Uana cogitatis, ideo uos ignis habebit. Haec Esaias ait. Tunc sic et ipsa maiestas, Cum esset in carne, profitetur ipse quis esset: Nemo meam animam potuit auferre conatus, Sed ego sponte eam pono a me meo decreto. Et sumendi iterum habeo potestatem in illam. Apertius autem de iusti morte clamatur, Ut pareat maius induratos esse Iudaeos: Ecce perit iustus, nec quidem intellegit ullus; Sed erit in pacem huius sepultura dilecti. Quid illi infamant in puteum esse dimissum, Cum legimus illum sepulturae traditum esse? Ignominiosi, crudeles, caeci, superbi, Qui magis de facto deberent lugere, plaudent! Inspiratus enim Salomon de ipso prophetat Et magis insequitur plenius ostendere iustum: Circumueniamus iustum, si [qui] nobis grauis esse uidetur Qui nostris operibus contrarius ualde resistit; Exprobrat in totum nihil nostra lege teneri Adhuc et adfirmat filium Altissimi esse. Omnimodo reprobat et nugaces aestimat esse Abstinet et sese a nobis et in altera uadit; Nos immundos ait et innouat altera iusta Et sibi laetatur Dominum patrem esse caelorum. Ergo, si sermones illius sunt ueri, probemus; Temptemus hunc Deum uidentes, quid sit in illum Interrogemus eum omni cum tormento quietum, Condemnemus eum turpissima morte' dicentes Haec cum fecissent, capita suspensa mouebant: Saluum illum faciat pater, aut discendat abinde! Ut eos caecos Salomon ostendat aperte, Sic, quasi nunc referat, et fecisse talia culpat: Dum ista cogitant, ducti sunt in errore nefando Excaecauit illos malitia sua saeuire. Ecce quia caeci ipsi sunt et alteros aiunt Dixit illis Salomon: Nescierunt Dei secreta.

author: Commodian
english: Whatever all the earlier witnesses said was done in Christ. Or let them say it of another? If they want to do that very thing, cheating in the mouth, let them mock themselves — let them look with the crowd at him. Who was that just one of whom the prophets sang, when no one is just on earth unless he had come from heaven? For David the prince sinned by loving the girl; Solomon sinned too; and yet they repented. When these so famous and marked kings of theirs were not just, but themselves sang of the Just One, neither did Isaiah the seer say such things of himself — who was cut by the saw under king Manasseh. One was stoned, another slaughtered at the altars; Herod ordered another, shut up, to be beheaded. All the just seers were destroyed by other deaths — that the Lord hung on the wood, by Moses’ voice: ‘God is not hung like a man,’ he intimates beforehand; ‘or he does not suffer threats like a son of man,’ he says. So the Lord himself, when he had come, followed these: It is needful for me, he says, to be rejected by Moses’ voice. But I do not pluck all things, only the highest peaks, so that the unknowing may more easily learn true things. But these unjust, who seek to live by trickery, already once bloodstained, keep inventing empty things. They make fools more foolish by vanishing sayings — that he was crucified, when so it had to be for him. For so he arranged because of the first man’s ruin; not only for him, but for us too he came from heaven. He set a new people firm in his name; according to the prophecies Christ filled all things. Behold I make new things, Isaiah cries in him, and let no one recount former things or follow the old. These new things have gone forth today under our law; we nations believed in Christ by Moses’ saying. He had foretold two peoples would be, and indeed said the lesser people would excel. But those full of wickedness already in desperate rage: The law was given to us, they say; from where did you come? If they oppose us, they think they resist the Highest too, who willed to be good to us… ****** No earthly king is the Just One the prophets sang. Christ from heaven makes a new people; the lesser people excels — that is not ‘where did you come from?’

latin: Quaecumque dixerunt testes uniuersi priores In Christo fuerunt facta. Aut in altero dicant? Quod ipsum si cupiunt facere frustrantes in ore, Ipsi se subsannent, uideant cum plebem in illo. Quis fuit is iustus, de quo prophetae canebant, Cum nemo sit iustus in terris, nisi e caelo uenisset Dauid enim princeps peccauit amando puellam, Peccauit et Salomon; et tamen paenituit illos. Cum isti tam clari et insigni reges eorum Non fuerunt iusti, sed ipsi de iusto canebant, Nec quidem Esaias uates de se talia dixit, Qui fuit ab rege Manasse de serra secatus. Alter lapidatus, alter est mactatus ad aras, Alterum Herodes iussit decollari reclusum. Omnes iusti uates alia sunt morte perempti, Quod Dominus ligno pependit, uoce Moysi: 'Non quasi homo Deus suspenditur', intimat ante; 'Aut non ceu filius hominis minas patitur', inquit. Sic Dominus ipse cum uenisset, ista secutus: Oportet me, inquit, reprobari uoce Moysi. At ego non tota, sed summa fastigia carpo, Quo possint facilius ignorantes discere uera. Hi autem iniqui, <qui> subdole uiuere quaerunt, Iam semel cruenti perseuerant fingere uana. Infatuan<t> stultos maius euanescere dictis, Quod crucifixus, cum sic oporteret eundem. Sic enim disposuit propter primitiui ruinam; Non solum pro illo, et pro nobis uenit e caelo. Constituit populum nouum suo nomine firmum, Iuxta prophetias compleuit omnia Christus. Ecce noua facio, Esaias clamat in ipso, Et nemo priora reputet nec antiqua sequatur. Haec noua sunt hodie sub nostra lege profecta, gentes in Christo credi<di>mus dicto Moysi. Ille duos populos praedixerat esse futuros, Et quidem minorem populum praecellere dixit. Sed isti nequitiae pleni iam desperato furore: Lex nobis est data, dicunt, uos unde uenistis? Si nobis obsistunt, putant et resistere Summo, Qui uoluit nobis bonus esse .......

author: Commodian
english: Nor do those stiff-necked, bristles up, look at this: What? Always they tortured the innocent when the law was broken. So they did to God what they were used to, cruel, and still dare call themselves sons of the Highest. Already how the Lord rose I noted above — not from my voice, but I spoke prophetic sayings. But he had foretold the disciples all things about himself, how he would suffer from the people with Peter denying; and that he would rise from the tombs on the third day — he had said that too, and he filled all the sayings. But when he rose, he came to the apostles himself and stood in their midst: Peace to you, he says. Among which disciples one was not there praying; when they reported to him, he began to disbelieve and adds: If first I do not put my finger where the nails were, or where he was struck by the lance, I do not believe. Then on the Lord’s day he returned again to them and stood in their midst: Peace to you, he says. And at once he approaches that unbelieving Thomas: Come nearer and touch the body as before. I am not a shade, such as the dead are held to be: a shade makes no footprint; consider the wound. He stretched the palms; but that one began to touch and put the hand in the side where the lance had been fixed, and from then bowed himself praying: You are my God and Lord truly! Against whom: Because you have seen these things, you have believed, but those later ones are happy who believe by the name alone heard. Forty days in order he spent with them; he taught them many things that would come on the age. After his ascent they did many wonders; by the word they healed the sick in Christ’s name. If he were such as those faithless say, strong things would not happen from the witnesses’ word through him. He ascended into the heavens, as also scripture sang: Receive the king, princes, of the heavens on high! What more need is there to recite all things from the law? These suffice for the raw, to be kept with a good heart. But if they themselves will not know God by reading these things, let them reckon to themselves where they will have come — there where they do not will. ****** Third-day risen: Peace to you. Thomas touches; later ears are blessed. Forty days, ascent, healings in the Name — not a shade.

latin: Nec illud respiciunt ceruicosi, setis rectis Quid? semper innocuos cruciarunt lege uitata. Sic Deo fecerunt, quod erant consueti, crudeles, Et filios sese audent adhuc dicere Summi. Iam qualiter <dominus> resurrexit, supra notaui, Non de uoce mea, sed dicta prophetica dixi. Praedixerat autem discipulis cuncta de sese, Qualiter a populo pateretur Petro negante; Et quia de tumulis resurgeret tertio die, Dixerat et ipsud, et compleuit omnia dicta. At ubi surrexit, uenit ad apostolos ipse Et stetit illis in medio: Pax uobis, inquit. Inter quos discipulos non adfuit unus orantes; Cui cum referrent, discredere coepit et addit: Si prius non digitum misero, ubi claui fuerunt Aut ubi percussus de lancea, non ego credo. Tunc die Dominica rursus remeauit ad illos Et stetit illis in medio: Pax uobis, inquit. Et statim adgreditur Thomam incredulum illum: Accede propius et contange corpus ut ante. Non ego sum umbra, mortuorum qualis habetur: Uestigium umbra non facit; considera uulnus. Extendit palmas; at ille tangere coepit Et manum in latere, fuerat quod lancea fixa, Misit et exinde prostrauit se<se> precando: Tu Deus et Dominus uere meus! Contra quem Haec quia uidisti, credidis<ti>, sed illi felices Posteri, qui credunt audito nomine tantum. Quadraginta dies cum illis ex ordine fecit, Edocuit illis multa, quae saeculo uenirent. Post cuius ascensum miracula multa fecerunt, De uerbo curabant infirmos in nomine Christi. Qui si talis erat, qualem isti perfidi dicunt, Fortia non fierent testium de uerbo per illum. Ascendit in caelos, sicut et scriptura canebat: Excipite regem, principes, caelorum in altis! Quid amplius opus est recitare cuncta de lege? Sufficiunt ista rudibus, bono corde tuenda. Quod si nec ipsi uolunt scire Deum ista legendo, Ipsi sibi reputent, quo uenerint, illo quo nolunt.

author: Commodian
english: They do nothing but the heart; for the rest, about life it is silent. What helps to chase worldly things on earth in vain, and to know kings’ riches, their wars? And to know the mad forum, skilled in law — that rights wobble, lest by chance they be ruled by a bribe? Be he a defender, be he a divine orator: he will profit nothing by death if alive he denied in Christ. Rather let him first seek where his life has been brought back, if he will be wise; if the rest, he is blamed. They read laws and learn wondrous speeches, but they outdo the miserable for whom they speak by their doing. Unhappy is that one who has come into their mouth; they carry praises and he a victory by losses. The miserable stands mute in the middle, whom it hurts more inside; they thunder with the mouth and he with silence by coins. Meanwhile the adorned voice of the day makes a din, and often the better cause becomes bad by giving a little more. From here the wise seeks a price, from here he rejoices to win; even if he acts crookedly, while only he is victor, he is sick. He treats nothing of his own cause when he tries for gains; another’s hope comes over him and he casts his own behind. Many are seized from the age’s wood by success; while they rejoice in short things, they remain from Christ’s grace; while they desire many things with the eye, while they seek to increase, God is nothing to them except the age’s life. For the belly he busies himself; the day’s contest is for that itself, and he spurns the true contest for eternal salvation. Whoever as if watches for the sack is praised sharp; for who follows God is judged dung by them. O too happy, if anyone avoids worldly things! Let him be a fool to others, while he is wise to the most high God. That whole hope is to believe God, who hung on the wood; the thing may be foul, but useful for the future life. For that first people was deceived about him — that he said Son, when he is God, the ancient himself. He went before them in a column of cloud and fire when he freed them from Egypt to a one. He commands the cruel unspeakable about the only-born, that he might prove Abraham, to whom he said ‘Spare!’ from heaven — the angel. And he is God, and likewise made himself man… ****** Flee the forum’s short wins. Happy the fool-to-others who is wise to God: hope is believing the One who hung on the wood.

latin: Nil nisi cor faciunt, ceterum de uita siletur. Quid iuuat in uano saecularia prosequi terris, Et scire diuitiis regum, de bellis eorum? Insanumque forum cognoscere iure peritum, Quod iura uacillant, praemio ne forte regantur? Sit licet defensor, sit licet diuinus orator, Nil morte proficiet, si uiuus in Christo negauit. Immo prius quaerat, ubi sit sua uita redacta, Si fuerit sapiens; si ceterum, uituperatur. Illi legunt iura et discunt proloquia mira, Sed superant miseros, pro quibus loquuntur, agendo. Infelix est ille, qui uenerit illis in ore; Illi ferunt laudes et ille uictoria<m> damnis. Stat miser in medio mutus, cui plus dolet intus; Illi tonant ore et ille silentio nummis. Obstrepit interea uox adornata diurnum Et saepe fit causa melior mala pluscula dando. Hinc pretium quae<rit> sapiens, hinc uincere gaudet, Etsi praue gerat, dum sit modo uictor, aegrotat. Nil sua de causa tractat, cum lucra conatur; Spem subit alterius et sua posterga remittit. Multi de successu rapiuntur saeculi silua; Dum gaudent in breuia, remanent a gratia Christi; Dum cupiunt multa oculo, dum augere quaerunt, Nec Deus est illis aliquid nisi saeculi uita. Pro uentre satagit, agon est pro ipso diurnum, Et uerum agonem spernit pro aeterna salute. Quisque quasi uigilat sacculo, laudatur acutus; Nam qui Deum sequitur, copria iudicatur ab ipsis. O nimium felix, saecularia si quis euitet! Sit stultus aliis, sapiens dum sit Deo summo. Ipsa spes est tota, Deo credere, qui ligno pependit; Foeda licet res est, sed utilis uitae futurae. Nam populus ille primitiuus illo deceptus Quod filium dixit, cum sit Deus, pristinus ipse. Hic praeibat eos in columna nubis et ignis, Quando de Aegypto liberauit illos ad unum. Hic crudele nefas imperat de unico nato, Ut probaret Abraham, cui dixit 'Parce!' e caelo Angelus. Et Deus est, hominem totidemque se fecit,

author: Commodian
english: And whatever he wills, he will do, so that mute things speak. He made Balaam’s donkey speak to the one beating her, and the dog, that it might say to Simon: You are being cried out by Peter! That many might learn from Paul preaching, he made a lion speak to the people with a divine voice. Then — what our nature itself does not allow — he made an infant in the fifth month speak to the crowd. This one was going to come mixed with our blood, so that he would be seen as man, but God was hiding in flesh. Not an elder will come, nor an angel, Isaiah said, but the Lord himself will come to show himself to us. Him the sea feared, him the winds, him Tartarus itself; every creature recognized the hidden Lord. Only the wicked people raised a centuria against him: ‘Far be it that the Lord should have come in such a figure!’ He was going thus on earth over the waves of the sea and commands the winds to give back a calm plain. He broke the Tartarean law by his present word and raises Lazarus from the tombs on the fourth day, stinking. For the one who was being carried, when he had met him: Rise, youth! he says. And that one rose from the bier. The synagogue-ruler’s daughter, begged from the father, already lifeless, he raises for those mourning her. He made the mute speak and the deaf hear especially, and the blind born from the womb, that he might see into the airs. After thirty-eight years he ordered a paralytic to rise, whom they would admire carrying the cot on his neck. … By touch of whose garment she was healed of a flow. He broke five loaves among five thousand men and again refreshed four thousand from seven. More fully that the Lord might show himself present, he had been invited to a wedding with his own mother; asked to help when wine failed, then he ordered the jars filled faster with water, which he first tasted and so commanded to be served. Nor so could they recognize the Lord by deeds, but they raged, as if a wicked man, to destroy him by death. Which he himself grants, since he decreed to suffer so — if yet they believe, then at last they will have pardon. This is the firstborn foretold beforehand through the prophets, that he be called on earth the Most High’s offspring. Happy those of men who place their hope in this one — for the foolish avoid him as a curse. Eternity is prepared for that one who believes Christ, so that man may be God’s partner living after funerals. Law and prophets teach who are worthy of the God of the heavens, and to whom the golden ages hidden are revealed. Through so many seers in number it is cried about God’s Son, and the first-called sons of God closed their eyes — ****** God hid in flesh; creation knew him. Seas, tombs, bread, wedding-jars — and still they raged. Happy who plant hope in this one.
